## Query Recipes

Example queries you can run against this knowledge base using the ranking engine:

```
# Find files most relevant to a concept
readmenator query "Where is the import resolver implemented?"

# Rank files by relevance to a topic
readmenator query "How does documentation generation work?"

# Explain why a file ranks highly
readmenator query "explain readmenator/_documentation.py"

# Trace dependency paths with ranked context
readmenator query "path from CLI to exporter"
```

The ranking model uses the following signals:

- **Personalized PageRank** (45% weight): query-specific relevance via seed propagation
- **Global Authority** (20% weight): structural importance via standard PageRank
- **Test Coverage** (15% weight): fraction of symbols referenced in test files
- **Doc Coverage** (10% weight): presence of docstrings and file-level docs
- **Freshness** (10% weight): recent modification activity

Results include score decomposition and justification paths for each ranked item.

{"doc": "moonshine-download-smoke: a tiny CLI used by scripts/test-model-downloads.sh to verify that the native download manifests are complete. It has two modes:  moonshine-download-smoke manifest <modality> [spec...] Prints one \"<url>\\t<relative_path>\" line per required file, resolved from the C API dependency functions (the single source of truth). The bash harness downloads each url into <root>/<relative_path>.  moonshine-download-smoke run <modality> <root> [spec...] Loads the engine from the freshly downloaded <root> and runs one trivial inference, exiting 0 on success. If a required file was missing from the manifest, loading or inference fails here - which is exactly what this test is meant to catch.  Modalities and their [spec...] arguments: stt    <language> [<model_arch>] intent <model_name> <variant> tts    <language> <voice> g2p    <language>  HTTP lives entirely in the bash harness (curl); this tool never touches the network. It only resolves manifests and exercises the on-disk load path.  include <cstdint> include <cstdio> include <cstdlib> include <cstring> include <cmath> include <filesystem> include <iostream>", "id": This is the C++ port of the tables that previously lived only in python/src/moonshine_voice/download.py, promoted here so every language binding resolves the exact same download manifest from a single source of truth. The TTS / G2P dependency catalog lives separately under core/moonshine-tts/ and is surfaced by moonshine_get_tts_dependencies / moonshine_get_g2p_dependencies; this file covers the remaining model types.  include <cstdint> include <optional> include <string> include <vector>", "id": "core/moonshine-model-catalog.h", "kind": "module", "label": "moonshine-model-catalog.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "fd35e30c2cb60a0c", "symbol_count": 8, "symbols": [{"doc": "One set of files that share a single base URL. When `include_spelling` is true and a spelling model is published for the language, a second group carrying the spelling files is appended.  Returns std::nullopt if the language (or the language+arch combination) is unknown.", "kind": "function", "line": 44, "name": "stt_model_dependencies", "signature": "std::optional<ModelDependencies> stt_model_dependencies( const std::string& language, std::optional<int32_t> model_arch, bool include_spelling);"}, {"doc": "Returns the download manifest for an intent-recognition embedding model.  `model_name` is an embedding model id (e.g. \"embeddinggemma-300m\"). `variant` is one of the published variants (\"q4\", \"q8\", \"fp16\", \"fp32\", \"q4f16\"); an empty string selects the model's default variant. Ported from the standalone ``custom_ops/swoosh_op.cc`` in the ZipVoice repo. The only structural change is that these kernels are compiled *into* libmoonshine (which already links onnxruntime) and registered on a session directly via ``zipvoice_register_custom_ops`` rather than being built as a separate shared library that ORT ``dlopen``s at runtime. This avoids loading a .so/.dll, which some platforms (e.g. iOS) make difficult.  SwooshL / SwooshR: the Zipformer activations. Exported to ONNX they decompose into ~11 element-wise nodes each; these ops collapse each activation into a single kernel. softplus(z) = log(1 + exp(z)) = max(z, 0) + log1p(exp(-|z|)) SwooshL(x)  = softplus(x - 4.0) - 0.08 * x - 0.035 SwooshR(x)  = softplus(x - 1.0) - 0.08 * x - 0.313261687 GluGate: out[..., c] = x[..., c] * sigmoid(x[..., C + c]),  C = lastdim / 2 DepthwiseConv1d: fuses Transpose -> depthwise Conv1d ('same' pad K//2) -> Transpose in [T,N,C]. BiasNorm: RMS-style norm of (x - bias) over channels, scaled by exp(log_scale). Bypass: per-channel residual lerp src_orig + (src - src_orig) * scale.  include \"zipvoice-custom-ops.h\"  include <algorithm> include <cmath> include <cstddef> include <vector>", "id": "Reliability-only escape hatch: when the MOONSHINE_ORT_SINGLE_THREAD environment variable is set to a non-empty value other than \"0\", force this session to run entirely on the calling thread (intra-op = inter-op = 1, sequential execution) so onnxruntime spawns no internal thread pool.  This is intended solely for running the library under ThreadSanitizer, whose interceptors deadlock inside onnxruntime's uninstrumented thread-pool synchronization. Production builds never set the variable, so this is a no-op there with zero performance impact. Call immediately after CreateSessionOptions.", "kind": "function", "line": 104, "name": "ort_maybe_force_single_thread", "signature": "void ort_maybe_force_single_thread(const OrtApi *ort_api, OrtSessionOptions *session_options);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 106, "name": "ort_parse_provider_names", "signature": "std::vector<std::string> ort_parse_provider_names(const std::string &csv);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 108, "name": "ort_append_execution_providers", "signature": "OrtStatus *ort_append_execution_providers( const OrtApi *ort_api, OrtSessionOptions *session_options, const std::vector<std::string> &provider_names, const OrtExecutionProviderOptions *config);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 125, "name": "LOG_ORT_ERROR", "signature": "LOG_ORT_ERROR(ort_api, ort_append_execution_providers(ort_api, session_options, provider_names, &config));"}, {"kind": "macro", "line": 2, "name": "ORT_UTILS_H", "signature": "#define ORT_UTILS_H"}, {"kind": "macro", "line": 18, "name": "RETURN_ON_ORT_ERROR", "signature": "#define RETURN_ON_ORT_ERROR(ort_api, expr)"}, {"kind": "macro", "line": 29, "name": "LOG_ORT_ERROR", "signature": "#define LOG_ORT_ERROR(ort_api, expr)"}, {"kind": "macro", "line": 81, "name": "ORT_RUN", "signature": "#define ORT_RUN(ort_api, session, input_names, inputs, input_count,         \\\n                output_names, output_count, outputs)"}]}, {"doc": "libFuzzer harness for the binary tokenizer.  The in-memory BinTokenizer constructor parses an untrusted byte blob (a tokenizer.bin loaded from disk or an app bundle), so it is a natural fuzz target. We first build a tokenizer from the raw input, then round-trip a slice of the same input through text_to_tokens / tokens_to_text. Exceptions are the library's documented failure mode, so they are caught and ignored; only sanitizer errors (out-of-bounds reads, leaks, UB) fail the run.  include <algorithm> include <cstddef> include <cstdint> include <exception> include <string> include <vector>  include \"bin-tokenizer.h\"", "id": "core/reliability/fuzz-bin-tokenizer.cpp", "kind": "module", "label": "fuzz-bin-tokenizer.cpp", "language": "cpp", "sha256": "b60848d181e5e4ac", "symbol_count": 2, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 21, "name": "tokenizer", "signature": "BinTokenizer tokenizer(data, size);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 25, "name": "text", "signature": "const std::string text(data, data + text_size);"}]}, {"doc": "libFuzzer harness for the audio resampler. The shape/dtype/data constructor forwards to moonshine_tensor_from_shape_and_dtype, which turns an (attacker-influenced) shape into an element count, a byte size, an allocation, and a memcpy. A crafted shape can overflow the size arithmetic; this harness feeds arbitrary dimensions (including huge values whose product overflows) so ASan/UBSan catch any regression in the overflow handling. Unsupported dtypes throw by design, so construction is wrapped; only sanitizer errors fail the run.  include <cstddef> include <cstdint> include <exception> include <vector>  include \"moonshine-tensor-view.h\"", "id": "core/reliability/fuzz-tensor-view.cpp", "kind": "module", "label": "fuzz-tensor-view.cpp", "language": "cpp", "sha256": "4b87e73207a9bb5e", "symbol_count": 5, "symbols": [{"doc": "Minimal sequential reader over the fuzz input; out-of-bytes reads yield zero.", "kind": "struct", "line": 21, "name": "Reader"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 25, "name": "next_u8", "signature": "uint8_t next_u8()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 27, "name": "next_i64", "signature": "int64_t next_i64()"}, {"doc": "8 bytes/element is the widest dtype, so this source is always at least as large as the copy the constructor performs.", "kind": "function", "line": 82, "name": "source", "signature": "std::vector<uint8_t> source(element_count * 8, 0);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 83, "name": "view", "signature": "MoonshineTensorView view(shape, dtype, source.data(), \"fuzz\");"}]}, {"doc": "libFuzzer harness for the WAV/RIFF parsers. The transcriber has a long-stream memory test (transcriber-streaming-memory- test.cpp); this is the TTS analogue. It exercises each available engine (Kokoro, Piper, ZipVoice, English only) through the public C API in two loops that probe the two distinct leak surfaces:  * \"synth\"  - one synthesizer, many moonshine_text_to_speech() calls (each output buffer freed). Catches leaks in the inference / G2P / per-call allocation path. * \"reload\" - repeatedly create and free the synthesizer handle. Catches leaks in model load / teardown and the handle table.  TTS exposes no internal retained-byte accessor (unlike the transcriber's stream_vad_completed_audio_bytes), so the signal here is process RSS: the test samples resident memory after every iteration and fails on sustained, post-warmup growth using the same regression heuristic as the transcriber test. onnxruntime arena allocators grow during warmup and then plateau, so the warmup window is skipped and only a persistent upward trend is treated as a regression.  The bundled TTS data (core/moonshine-tts/data) is required. Pass its path as argv[1], or run with a working directory from which it can be discovered (repo root, test-assets/, or core/build). Engines whose assets are absent are skipped. We disambiguate \"harmless reboot race\" from \"real failure\" by checking whether the volume disappears shortly after.  Progress: we run cp in the background and poll the destination file size against the source size. The RP2350 throttles USB mass-storage writes (the bootrom flashes each block before ACKing), so the growing dest size is a faithful progress signal. Solves four problems with using `screen` directly:  1. `screen` exits immediately if the tty doesn't exist yet -- so if you flash and then type the screen command, you race the Pico's USB enumeration and lose the first batch of output. 2. `screen` exits on a brief device drop, which happens any time the firmware is reset (BOOTSEL re-entered, watchdog reboot, power cycle, USB hub glitch, ...). 3. By the time you'd notice and re-run screen, the boot banner and per-clip lines have already been printed and discarded. 4. `screen` is a full-screen TUI -- you lose the parent shell, can't tee to a logfile easily, and Ctrl-C doesn't exit it (you have to remember Ctrl-A k y).  CRITICAL: on macOS we MUST use /dev/cu.usbmodem*, NOT /dev/tty.usbmodem*. The two paths point at the same underlying USB CDC device, but the kernel handles open() very differently:  /dev/tty.usbmodem*  - \"modem callin\" device. open() blocks until the device asserts DCD (carrier detect). Pico TinyUSB CDC never drives the modem control lines, so this open() hangs FOREVER, `cat` reads zero bytes, the log file stays empty, and the script looks completely broken even though the firmware is happily printing. This bit us hard once already. /dev/cu.usbmodem*   - \"callout\" device. open() returns immediately regardless of modem control state. The device stops draining USB\nwhile it does STT + TTS (it isn't reading hops then), so a *blocking* write\nwould park the sender thread in an uninterruptible kernel os.write -- and a\nblocking read would do the same to the reader thread when the device is\nquiet. On macOS that uninterruptible state survives Ctrl-C and wedges the\nCDC handle until you physically replug. With O_NONBLOCK, os.write/os.read\nraise BlockingIOError (EAGAIN) instead of blocking, so both threads stay\nresponsive and shutdown is always clean. WS-HOP) stays at its initial zeros, so the STT only ever sees the single newest 32 ms hop (silence at kSpeechEnd) -- i.e. \"silence + a tiny burst at the end\", rms ~0. The host (examples/rp2350/scripts/usb_audio_bridge.py) captures the laptop mic at 16 kHz and streams it to the device as framed 32 ms hops over USB CDC. The device runs the streaming VAD on those hops; when a speech segment ends it front-aligns the 1 s clip, classifies it with the SpellingCNN, sends the result back, and speaks the recognized letter/digit via the formant TTS, streaming that PCM back to the host to play on the laptop speaker.  VAD (~36 KiB arena), the SpellingCNN classifier (~366 KiB arena) and the TTS synth (arena working memory) never run at the same time, so they reuse the SINGLE tensor arena sequentially (Vad -> Classifier -> StreamSynth -> Vad). `window` is the reused 1 s int16 waveform buffer (g_waveform) that doubles as the sliding capture window and the front-aligned STT clip; no extra big SRAM buffer is allocated. int16 (vs fp32) halves it to 32 KiB; the VAD + STT front-ends convert to float at the read site.  ifndef SPELLING_AUDIO_SERVICE_H_ define SPELLING_AUDIO_SERVICE_H_  include <cstddef> include <cstdint>  include \"audio_io.h\"", "id": "micro/examples/rp2350/src/audio_service.h", "kind": "module", "label": "audio_service.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "e94479edbb0cd8cd", "symbol_count": 8, "symbols": [{"kind": "struct", "line": 26, "name": "kiss_fftr_state"}, {"doc": "Build the persistent recognizer front-end (the streaming VAD mel front-end, the STT log-mel, and their shared 512-pt FFT). Unlike the microphone input (whose absolute level we can't choose, and which RecognizeOne RMS-normalizes before the STT front-end so the quiet I2S mic clears the log-mel eps floor), the TTS reply is OUR signal: the streaming synth already self-normalizes each utterance to ~-1 dBFS (VoiceParams::output_gain + a soft limiter), so its peak is predictable. That makes \"volume\" a clean scalar we get to pick: 1.0 plays at full scale (loudest, and cleanest on a small speaker, which needs the whole range to stay above the noise floor); values < 1.0 attenuate. Values > 1.0 are allowed but will clip the already-near-full-scale reply, so prefer <= 1.0. 175, "name": "dma_channel_abort", "signature": "dma_channel_abort(dma_chan_);"}]}, {"doc": "I2S speaker output for the on-board echo service (MAX98357A / Adafruit 3006).  Wiring (matches src/i2s_out.pio; LRC = BCLK + 1 for the sideset pair): DIN -> GPIO10   BCLK <- GPIO11   LRC <- GPIO12   Vin -> VSYS   GND -> GND  The MAX98357A has its own I2S DAC + reconstruction filter, so this backend just feeds int16 PCM straight to a PIO I2S transmitter -- no PWM carrier, no RC filter, and no output EQ. Each mono sample is written into BOTH I2S slots so the amp's default (L+R)/2 mix plays it at full level.  A DMA-fed ring buffer decouples the (bursty) producer from the (steady) I2S consumer. The neural-TTS engine emits audio in bursts -- it goes silent for ~240 ms while it decodes a tile, then renders that tile out in a rush -- so feeding the 8-deep PIO FIFO directly with blocking writes starved it during every decode pause and chopped the speech into stuttering fragments (~36% of a sentence came out as gaps). Instead, Write() drops frames into a ~0.5 s ring that a free-running DMA drains into the PIO TX FIFO at exactly the sample rate (DREQ-paced, read-address auto-wrapped). Playback starts once the ring has pre-buffered enough to ride out a decode pause, and because synthesis is (just) faster than real-time the ring stays fed, so the audio plays smoothly.  ifndef SPELLING_I2S_AUDIO_OUT_H_ define SPELLING_I2S_AUDIO_OUT_H_  include <cstdint>  include \"audio_io.h\" include \"hardware/pio.h\"", "id": "micro/examples/rp2350/src/i2s_audio_out.h", "kind": "module", "label": "i2s_audio_out.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "7e3734befbc7fef8", "symbol_count": 10, "symbols": [{"kind": "class", "line": 42, "name": "I2sAudioOutput"}, {"doc": "Linear playback gain applied before I2S conversion. Designed for the Adafruit MAX98357A I2S class-D amp (#3006, https://www.adafruit.com/product/3006), which has its own I2S DAC -- so unlike the old PWM speaker there is no carrier and no RC reconstruction filter. Connect your own 4-8 ohm speaker to the amp's screw terminals.  Wiring (see src/i2s_out.pio; LRC = BCLK + 1 for the sideset pair):  Vin  -> Pico VSYS   (physical pin 39)   ; 2.5-5.5 V; use VSYS not VBUS GND  -> Pico GND    (physical pin 38) DIN  -> GP10        (physical pin 14)   ; I2S data BCLK -> GP11        (physical pin 15)   ; bit clock LRC  -> GP12        (physical pin 16)   ; word select (LRCLK) GAIN -> (leave open -> 9 dB)   SD -> (leave open -> enabled, (L+R)/2 mono)  GP10/11/12 are chosen so they don't collide with the I2S mic test (GP0/1/2). It does NOT touch the VAD/STT/TTS pipeline -- it only proves that an Adafruit SPH0645 I2S MEMS mic (https://www.adafruit.com/product/3421) is wired up and producing audio.  Wiring (matches the arduino-pico I2SInput.ino example the user followed):  mic DOUT -> GPIO0   (data into the RP2350) mic BCLK <- GPIO1   (bit clock, driven by the RP2350) mic LRCL <- GPIO2   (word select; must be BCLK + 1 for the PIO sideset) mic SEL  -> GND     (puts the mono element on the LEFT channel) mic GND  <-> GND mic 3V   <-> 3V3 (OUT)  Each cycle: record 5 s at 16 kHz, print per-channel stats, then (if USB is connected) stream the clip to the host for 5 s of playback. This firmware does NO synthesis, VAD or STT. It is the device half of the hardware-in-the-loop TTS eval harness (scripts/hw_tts_eval/): the laptop synthesizes speech, streams the raw PCM here over USB CDC, and this app plays it out the MAX98357A I2S amp so an external mic can record the real acoustic path. Keeping the device dumb means the loop measures the exact same I2sAudioOutput path the live apps use, with nothing else in the way.  Wiring (identical to moonshine_micro_i2s_audio_test; see src/i2s_out.pio): Vin  -> Pico VSYS (pin 39)   GND -> GND DIN  -> GP10   BCLK -> GP11   LRC -> GP12   (MAX98357A / Adafruit 3006) GAIN -> open (9 dB)   SD -> open (enabled, (L+R)/2 mono)  Protocol (line commands over CDC; binary PCM is framed, not line-based): PING              -> replies \"PONG\" PLAY <rate> <n>   -> then read `n` int16 LE samples, streamed in hops of up to kHop samples, each hop prefixed by the 0xA5 0x5A sync (mirrors usb_audio_io.cc). Samples are written to I2sAudioOutput at <rate> Hz. When done, replies \"PLAYED <m>\" with the number of samples actually played (m == n on a clean stream).  PICO_STDIO_DEFAULT_CRLF=0 (see CMakeLists.txt) keeps 0x0A/0x0D PCM bytes from being mangled on the way in, and keeps our text replies from getting CR injected on the way out.  include <cstdint> include <cstdio> include <cstdlib>", "id": "micro/examples/rp2350/src/main_i2s_relay.cc", "kind": "module", "label": "main_i2s_relay.cc", "language": "cc", "sha256": "189bef8823d4ddea", "symbol_count": 20, "symbols": [{"doc": "Read one newline-terminated line into `buf` (NUL-terminated), blocking until a non-empty line arrives. Feeds the watchdog each idle slice. CR and LF both terminate; blank lines are skipped.", "kind": "function", "line": 71, "name": "ReadLine", "signature": "int ReadLine(char* buf, int maxlen)"}, {"doc": "Read one byte, waiting up to ~timeout_ms. Returns -1 on timeout.", "kind": "function", "line": 88, "name": "ReadByteTimed", "signature": "int ReadByteTimed(int timeout_ms)"}, {"doc": "Scan for the 0xA5 0x5A sync, then read up to `n` int16 LE samples into `out`. Returns the number of samples read; a short return means the host stalled mid-hop (each sample byte read times out so a dropped frame can't wedge the device -- see the deadlock note in usb_audio_io.cc). Returns -1 if no sync arrives within ~2 s (host aborted the stream).", "kind": "function", "line": 98, "name": "ReadHop", "signature": "int ReadHop(int16_t* out, int n)"}, {"doc": "Receive `total` samples from the host into RAM, then play them to the I2S amp at `rate` Hz. Returns the number of samples played.  Why buffer the whole clip instead of streaming hop->FIFO directly: the PIO I2S TX FIFO is only a few frames deep, and reading a 512-sample hop over USB CDC (one getchar per byte) takes far longer than those few frames play out. A read-then-write loop therefore underruns the FIFO on every hop boundary -- the SM stalls mid-stream and the amp clicks, which sounds like continuous broadband static. Receiving the whole clip first (no real-time constraint; USB flow-control backpressures the host) then streaming RAM->FIFO keeps the FIFO fed faster than real time, so playback is glitch-free.", This is what lets you separate the kernel>1 stem CONV_2D from the 1x1 pointwise CONV_2D instances (all tagged \"CONV_2D\" by TFLM).", "kind": "function", "line": 33, "name": "printf", "signature": "printf(\"[prof:%s] --- per-op (execution order) ---\\n\", label);"}]}, {"doc": "Lightweight per-op profiler for the moonshine-micro SpellingCNN build.  Why not tflite::MicroProfiler? The stock implementation statically allocates kMaxEvents=4096 entries across four parallel arrays (~80 KB of SRAM). The RP2350 build runs with only ~20 KB of static margin, so the stock profiler simply doesn't fit. Our model executes only a few dozen ops per Invoke(), so a tiny fixed-capacity recorder is plenty.  This records, per Invoke(): * one (tag, microseconds) sample per op INSTANCE, in execution order -- so individual conv layers are distinguishable, e.g. the kernel>1 stem CONV_2D vs the many 1x1 pointwise CONV_2D instances (TFLM gives them all the \"CONV_2D\" tag, so per-instance order is the only way to tell them apart), * a per-tag total, so you get the \"where does the time go across op TYPES\" rollup (CONV_2D vs DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D vs ADD vs ...).  Timing uses the RP2350's free-running 64-bit microsecond timer (time_us_64), which is driven from a fixed reference clock and so is unaffected by any sys-clock overclock. BeginEvent/EndEvent each cost a couple of timer reads (sub-microsecond), negligible against the millisecond-scale ops being measured.  ifndef SPELLING_OP_PROFILER_H_ define SPELLING_OP_PROFILER_H_  include <cstdint>  include \"tensorflow/lite/micro/micro_profiler_interface.h\"", "id": "micro/examples/rp2350/src/op_profiler.h", "kind": "module", "label": "op_profiler.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "5cd9f0efc2fe9409", "symbol_count": 4, "symbols": [{"doc": "Drop all recorded events (call before each Invoke you want to measure in isolation).", "kind": "function", "line": 46, "name": "Reset", "signature": "void Reset()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 50, "name": "num_events", "signature": "int num_events() const"}, {"doc": "Print the per-instance and per-tag breakdown over USB stdio. `label` is prefixed to each line so multiple reports can be told apart.", "kind": "function", "line": 55, "name": "Report", "signature": "void Report(const char* label) const;"}, {"kind": "macro", "line": 26, "name": "SPELLING_OP_PROFILER_H_", "signature": "#define SPELLING_OP_PROFILER_H_"}]}, {"doc": "Spoken \"sound-alike\" word for each recognized class label, so the readback TTS says \"bee\" for 'b' rather than an unvoiceable bare consonant.  Based on the project's letter-name table (LETTER_TO_SPELLED in scripts/extract_aligned_letter_clips.py), but using real English words rather than that table's forced-aligner transliterations wherever a homophone of the letter name exists -- the formant TTS's G2P pronounces real words far more reliably. So H is \"aitch\" (not \"aich\"), R is \"are\" (not \"ar\"), W is \"double u\" (not \"dublu\"), X is \"ex\" (not \"eks\"). S is \"eh s\": a short vowel (\"eh\" -> /ɛ/) then the letter name (\"s\" -> /ɛs/ via the baked dictionary), which keeps the readback distinct from \"eff\" (/ɛf/) and bare /s/ hiss. A is \"hay\" (/heɪ/): there is no zero-onset English word for the letter-A vowel, and \"ay\"/\"a\" come out as \"eye\"/\"uh\" through the G2P, so we accept \"eye\"/\"uh\" through the G2P, so we accept the soft leading breath. E keeps the phonetic \"ee\" (no clean homophone). Digits already arrive as words (\"zero\"..\"nine\") and are spoken as-is.  ifndef SPELLING_SPELLING_LABELS_H_ define SPELLING_SPELLING_LABELS_H_", "id": "micro/examples/rp2350/src/spelling_labels.h", "kind": "module", "label": "spelling_labels.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "bf6cd448974793d5", "symbol_count": 2, "symbols": [{"doc": "Map a class label to the text the TTS should speak. After the spelling-recognition sweep finishes, the app hands its (now-idle) TFLM tensor arena to this service, which drops into a USB CDC command loop driving the neural TTS engine (neural-tts/, diphone units + RVQ decoder + WORLD-lite vocoder; fixed 16 kHz output):  host -> \"SPEAK the quick brown fox\\n\"   (on-device G2P) host -> \"IPA  h\\xC9\\x99lo\\xCA\\x8A\\n\"     (raw IPA, bypasses G2P)  device -> \"AUDIO <sample_rate> <num_samples>\\n\"   (framing header) device -> <num_samples * int16 little-endian PCM bytes> device -> \"\\nEND <num_samples>\\n\"  The sample count in the header is exact: the engine runs its deterministic planning passes first (EstimateSamples), then streams PCM as it renders. Backs two targets that differ ONLY in their audio backend (needs a Pico 2 W / CYW43, -DPICO_BOARD=pico2_w): * moonshine_micro_echo_wifi          USB audio bridge   [main_wifi.cc] * moonshine_micro_echo_wifi_hardware I2S mic + PWM spkr  [wifi_hardware_app.cc]  Reuses the same VAD -> STT -> TTS pipeline as the default echo service (RecognizeOne / Speak in audio_service.h), but drives a small state machine instead of echoing single letters: the user says \"wifi\", spells an SSID and password character-by-character (letters, digits, the symbol words, and the \"capital\"/\"delete\"/\"finish\"/\"cancel\"/\"yes\"/\"no\" command words the model already knows), the device joins the network over CYW43, and \"ip\" reads the assigned address back via TTS.  ifndef SPELLING_WIFI_APP_H_ define SPELLING_WIFI_APP_H_  include \"audio_io.h\"  // AudioInput / AudioOutput", "id": "micro/examples/rp2350/src/wifi_app.h", "kind": "module", "label": "wifi_app.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "0a1491b7f4a85a87", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "macro", "line": 15, "name": "SPELLING_WIFI_APP_H_", "signature": "#define SPELLING_WIFI_APP_H_"}]}, {"doc": "include \"wifi_hardware_app.h\"  include <cstdio>  include \"audio_config.h\"   // kVadSampleRate (via vad_config), kClipNumSamples include \"i2s_audio_io.h\"   // I2sAudioInput include \"i2s_audio_out.h\"  // I2sAudioOutput include \"vad_config.h\"     // kVadSampleRate include \"wifi_app.h\"       // RunWifiAppWithIo (shared setup state machine)", "id": "micro/examples/rp2350/src/wifi_hardware_app.cc", "kind": "module", "label": "wifi_hardware_app.cc", "language": "cc", "sha256": "7e7e39ec68db1f18", "symbol_count": 6, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 12, "name": "RunWifiHardwareApp", "signature": "void RunWifiHardwareApp()"}, {"doc": "Same wiring as the hardware echo app: I2S mic on GP0/1/2, I2S amp on DIN=GP10/BCLK=GP11/LRC=GP12. Identical setup flow to the default wifi app (see wifi_app.h): it reuses the shared RunWifiAppWithIo() state machine and only swaps the audio backend for I2sAudioInput + I2sAudioOutput. Needs a Pico 2 W / CYW43 board (-DPICO_BOARD=pico2_w).  ifndef SPELLING_WIFI_HARDWARE_APP_H_ define SPELLING_WIFI_HARDWARE_APP_H_", "id": "micro/examples/rp2350/src/wifi_hardware_app.h", "kind": "module", "label": "wifi_hardware_app.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "faf670d7c7b10437", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "macro", "line": 10, "name": "SPELLING_WIFI_HARDWARE_APP_H_", "signature": "#define SPELLING_WIFI_HARDWARE_APP_H_"}]}, {"doc": "feature-generation -- portable, heap-free log-mel spectrogram front-end.  This is the single public header for the module. It exposes two front-ends Slaney mel / periodic-Hann / kissfft real-FFT maths shared by both front-ends:  * LogMelSpectrogram -- a one-shot (\"batch\") front-end. Given a whole waveform it produces a normalised (n_mels x target_frames) log-mel feature plane. Used by the STT classifier.  * MelStreamer -- a streaming front-end for always-on use. It keeps the last `window_frames` log-mel columns in a ring and computes exactly ONE FFT per pushed hop, then rebuilds the normalised (n_mels x window_frames) model input. Used by the VAD, where the window slides one non-overlapping n_fft-sample block per inference.  Reflect-pad (center=true), windowed STFT, squared magnitude, Slaney mel filterbank, crop to frames, log(value + eps), per-clip mean/std standardisation (Bessel-corrected std clamped >= 1e-3).  Dependencies: kissfft (real FFT) and TFLM's micro_log (MicroPrintf, used only on fatal misconfiguration). No app, VAD, or STT dependencies -- so the module can be reused by any front-end on any platform that provides those two.  Memory: both front-ends are heap-free when handed precomputed flash tables. Per-call FFT scratch lives in a shared .bss pool (see src/fft_scratch.h), NOT on the stack, because the RP2350 gives each core only a 4 KB scratch-bank stack and a ~5 KB FFT frame would overflow it into the other core's stack.  ifndef FEATURE_GENERATION_FEATURE_GENERATION_H_ define FEATURE_GENERATION_FEATURE_GENERATION_H_", "id": "micro/feature-generation/include/feature_generation/feature_generation.h", "kind": "module", "label": "feature_generation.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "142e260f7e1aa199", "symbol_count": 23, "symbols": [{"doc": "Forward-declare kissfft's opaque real-FFT config so this header doesn't pull in kiss_fft.h. The .cc files own the actual lifecycle.", "kind": "struct", "line": 38, "name": "kiss_fftr_state"}, {"kind": "struct", "line": 64, "name": "LogMelParams"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 98, "name": "LogMelSpectrogram"}, {"doc": "-------------------------------------------------------------------------- Streaming front-end: MelStreamer. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------  Exactness: with hop == n_fft (non-overlapping blocks, center=false), after pushing N full blocks BuildModelInput() produces the SAME tensor LogMelSpectrogram::Compute(center=false) would over those N*n_fft samples (verified by tests/stream_parity_test).  Memory: one ring of n_mels*window_frames floats (<= 4 KB at the VAD's 32x32 bound) + the shared .bss FFT scratch. No heap.", "kind": "class", "line": 164, "name": "MelStreamer"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 119, "name": "n_mels", "signature": "int n_mels() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 121, "name": "target_frames", "signature": "int target_frames() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 122, "name": "n_freq", "signature": "int n_freq() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 123, "name": "params", "signature": "const LogMelParams& params() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 185, "name": "filled", "signature": "int filled() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 187, "name": "n_mels", "signature": "int n_mels() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 188, "name": "window_frames", "signature": "int window_frames() const"}, {"doc": "Periodic Hann window of length L (matches torch.hann_window(L, periodic=True)). Returns an empty vector when L <= 0.", "kind": "function", "line": 48, "name": "HannWindowPeriodic", "signature": "std::vector<float> HannWindowPeriodic(int length);"}, {"doc": "Slaney's auditory-toolbox mel scale (matches torchaudio _hz_to_mel(\"slaney\")).", "kind": "function", "line": 52, "name": "HzToMelSlaney", "signature": "float HzToMelSlaney(float hz);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 53, "name": "MelToHzSlaney", "signature": "float MelToHzSlaney(float mel);"}, {"doc": "Dense (n_mels, n_freq) Slaney-normalised triangular mel filterbank, row-major.", "kind": "function", "line": 57, "name": "MakeMelFilterbank", "signature": "std::vector<float> MakeMelFilterbank(int n_freq, int n_mels, int sample_rate, float f_min, float f_max);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 99, "name": "LogMelSpectrogram", "signature": "public: explicit LogMelSpectrogram(const LogMelParams& params);"}, {"doc": "Heap-free streaming compute. `waveform` is read-only; `out` must hold at least n_mels * target_frames floats. On return out[m * target_frames + t] is the normalised log-mel value for mel bin m, frame t. Frames that would require samples past the waveform are left at log(eps) (right-zero-pad).  Two input formats: fp32 in [-1, 1], or raw int16 mic samples converted to [-1, 1] at the read site (lets the caller store the 1 s clip as int16 and halve its SRAM -- the samples are int16-precision to begin with). WHY THIS EXISTS: on the RP2350 each core's stack is a single 4 KB scratch bank (core 0 -> SCRATCH_Y at 0x20081000, core 1 -> SCRATCH_X at 0x20080000, immediately below). A per-frame FFT working set of frame_buf[512] + spectrum[257] + power_row[257] is ~5 KB, and the historical \"upper bound\" sizes ([1024]/[513]) were ~10 KB. Placing that on the stack overflows core 0's 4 KB bank straight down into core 1's stack. CMSIS-NN runs a persistent dual-core GEMM worker on core 1 during TFLM Invoke(), so the two stacks collide and silently corrupt data -- which showed up as NaN VAD features and a garbage-initialised STT LogMelSpectrogram. See https://petewarden.com/2024/01/16/understanding-the-raspberry-pi-picos-memory-layout/  Keeping the scratch in .bss removes it from the stack entirely. Both the VAD mel streamer (MelStreamer::PushHop) and the STT front-end (LogMelSpectrogram::Compute) borrow this single pool. That is safe because they run ONLY on core 0, sequentially (VAD listening vs STT phase), and neither is ever re-entered.  ifndef FEATURE_GENERATION_FFT_SCRATCH_H_ define FEATURE_GENERATION_FFT_SCRATCH_H_  include \"kiss_fft.h\"  // kiss_fft_cpx", "id": "micro/feature-generation/src/fft_scratch.h", "kind": "module", "label": "fft_scratch.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "530f67bf5d7965ec", "symbol_count": 4, "symbols": [{"kind": "variable", "line": 31, "name": "g_fft_scratch_frame", "signature": "extern float g_fft_scratch_frame[kFftScratchNFft];"}, {"kind": "variable", "line": 33, "name": "g_fft_scratch_spec", "signature": "extern kiss_fft_cpx g_fft_scratch_spec[kFftScratchNFreq];"}, {"kind": "variable", "line": 34, "name": "g_fft_scratch_pow", "signature": "extern float g_fft_scratch_pow[kFftScratchNFreq];"}, {"kind": "macro", "line": 21, "name": "FEATURE_GENERATION_FFT_SCRATCH_H_", "signature": "#define FEATURE_GENERATION_FFT_SCRATCH_H_"}]}, {"doc": "Heap-free log-mel spectrogram for the on-device build.  Reflect-pad (center=True), windowed STFT, squared-magnitude, Slaney mel filterbank, crop to target_frames, log(value + eps), per-clip mean/std normalisation with std clamped >= 1e-3.  The DIFFERENCES from the desktop port are all about memory:  1. Compute() takes a caller-supplied output buffer instead of returning std::vector. Saves 64 KB of heap traffic per call.  2. Reflect padding is done on-the-fly per sample inside the framing loop. The desktop port materialised a 16512-sample `padded` vector (~66 KB).  3. STFT + power-spectrum + filterbank multiply are FUSED into a single pass: for each output frame we compute one 257-bin power row on the stack, then immediately scatter it through the mel filterbank into one column of the output buffer. The desktop port allocated a full (n_freq, n_frames) power matrix (~200 KB) and a (n_mels, n_frames) mel matrix (~64 KB).  4. log() and normalisation run in-place on the output buffer. Saves another 64 KB.  With our defaults this drops peak per-call heap usage from ~450 KB to 0 (just ~5 KB on the stack for frame_buf, spectrum, and one power row). The window + filterbank still live as heap std::vector members of LogMelSpectrogram itself (84 KB total), allocated ONCE in the constructor.", "id": "micro/feature-generation/src/log_mel.cc", "kind": "module", "label": "log_mel.cc", "language": "cc", "sha256": "0c4371e7537d7d34", "symbol_count": 23, "symbols": [{"doc": "Reflect index without duplicating the boundary. Matches torch.nn.functional.pad(x, (pad, pad), mode=\"reflect\"): index -1 -> 1, -2 -> 2, ..., and on the right side, n -> n-2, n+1 -> n-3, ...  `n` is the original waveform length, `i` is the padded-coords index in [-pad, n + pad). The implementation handles only the edge regions: callers in the hot loop pass already-validated indices in [0, n) directly past this helper. We use it from the framing loop where we sometimes step a sample or two past either edge due to center padding.", "kind": "function", "line": 69, "name": "ReflectIndex", "signature": "inline int ReflectIndex(int i, int n)"}, {"doc": "Per-sample input conversion for ComputeImpl. Pipeline per word: runtime override -> number normalizer -> baked common-word dictionary -> rule-based letter-to-sound. The result is IPA, folded to the synths' base-phone tokens by TokenizeIpa.  - Overrides:  g2p_dict.h  (user-supplied word->IPA, e.g. proper nouns) - Numbers:    src/g2p_numbers.h - Dictionary: g2p_dict.h + generated src/g2p_dict_data.h - Rules:      src/g2p_rules.h  The token vocabulary is shared by both TTS back ends (the Klatt formant synth in tts/ and the neural diphone synth in neural-tts/): one UTF-8 IPA base phone per token, plus \" \" (word gap), \".\" (sentence pause), and the stress marks \"ˈ\" / \"ˌ\" as their own tokens.  ifndef G2P_G2P_H_ define G2P_G2P_H_  include <string> include <vector>  include \"g2p_dict.h\"  // Lexicon", "id": "micro/g2p/include/g2p/g2p.h", "kind": "module", "label": "g2p.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "e4784ede04ba4c21", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"doc": "Convert plain English text to a flat list of base-phone tokens, including \" \" and \".\" pause tokens for word gaps and sentence breaks. `overrides`, if non-null, is consulted first.", "kind": "function", "line": 30, "name": "TextToPhones", "signature": "std::vector<std::string> TextToPhones(const std::string& text, const Lexicon* overrides = nullptr);"}, {"doc": "Split an IPA string into a sequence of base-phone tokens.  Handles multi-codepoint clusters: diphthongs (eɪ aɪ aʊ ɔɪ oʊ) and affricates (tʃ dʒ) are decomposed into their base symbols; length marks (ː) are dropped; a few common alternate symbols (ɚ ɡ r a y etc.) are folded to canonical keys. Unknown codepoints are skipped.  Stress marks (ˈ primary, ˌ secondary) are preserved as their own tokens so a synth can place pitch accents on the following vowel; they are not phones. Whitespace is preserved as the literal token \" \" so the caller can insert inter-word pauses.", "kind": "function", "line": 44, "name": "TokenizeIpa", "signature": "std::vector<std::string> TokenizeIpa(const std::string& ipa);"}, {"kind": "macro", "line": 18, "name": "G2P_G2P_H_", "signature": "#define G2P_G2P_H_"}]}, {"doc": "Baked common-word pronunciation dictionary + runtime override table. Lookups binary-search the blob directly in flash: no SRAM copy, only a little stack scratch. Each entry carries the data a Klatt-style cascade synthesizer needs: * a steady-state formant target (vowels / sonorants), or a formant \"locus\" the transition engine aims at (obstruents), * source amplitudes that decide what excites the resonators, and * an intrinsic duration that prosody later scales. synthesizer for the RP2350 (and desktop).  Unlike the batch Synthesize() (synth.h), which materializes the whole PCM waveform in a std::vector and peak-normalizes it, StreamSynth produces audio in arbitrary-length chunks on demand and never holds the full utterance:  * the second-largest buffer -- the per-frame parameter tracks -- lives in a caller-supplied arena (on the MCU this is the otherwise-idle TFLM tensor arena, since recognition and synthesis never run at the same time); * the largest buffer -- the PCM -- is never materialized; frames are rendered one at a time into a tiny scratch and copied into the caller's output buffer as Read() drains them.  Because the global peak isn't known while streaming, the final loudness stage differs from batch: a fixed VoiceParams::output_gain plus a soft limiter replace peak-normalization. Everything upstream (segments, smoothing, F0) is the shared, bit-identical code in synth_internal.*. This is the single public header for the module. Include only this; it pulls in the public synth types. The remaining headers under include/tts/ are the transitive implementation types that StreamSynth exposes by value (the Klatt resonators, the per-frame parameter tracks, the voice config); the G2P internals live privately in src/.  The core is intentionally self-contained: C++17, float-only math, small fixed state, no allocation in the audio inner loop, and NO third-party dependency (not even kissfft or TFLM). Only the streaming synthesis path used on the MCU is included here.  Typical use (the platform glue -- USB command loop, arena ownership -- lives in the example, not here):  tts::VoiceParams voice = tts::DefaultVoiceParams(); tts::StreamSynth synth(voice, arena, arena_size); tts::StreamOptions opts; opts.sample_rate = 22050.0f; synth.BeginText(\"hello world\", opts);          // or BeginIpa(...) float buf[256]; for (int n; (n = synth.Read(buf, 256)) > 0; )  // stream PCM, never buffers emit(buf, n);  ifndef TTS_TTS_H_ define TTS_TTS_H_  include \"config.h\"        // tts::VoiceParams, tts::DefaultVoiceParams include \"synth_stream.h\"  // tts::StreamSynth, StreamOptions, StreamStatus", "id": "micro/klatt-tts/include/tts/tts.h", "kind": "module", "label": "tts.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "f7a800d24c5503a0", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "macro", "line": 26, "name": "TTS_TTS_H_", "signature": "#define TTS_TTS_H_"}]}, {"doc": "include \"config.h\"  include <cstdio> include <fstream> include <sstream> include <string> include <unordered_map> include <vector>", "id": "micro/klatt-tts/src/config.cc", "kind": "module", "label": "config.cc", "language": "cc", "sha256": "b360fd208c796416", "symbol_count": 10, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 13, "name": "ClassName", "signature": "const char* ClassName(PhoneClass c)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 33, "name": "SourceName", "signature": "const char* SourceName(Source s)"}, {"doc": "Apply one \"<field> <value>\" override to a phone. on-device neural TTS engine.  Runs the EXACT C++ pipeline the RP2350 firmware runs -- shared g2p front end -> Klatt rule durations -> diphone/word unit selection -> int8 RVQ decode through the s16x8 TFLM graph -> WORLD-lite vocoder -- but on the host, using the portable TFLM reference kernels (see host/tflm_ref/) instead of CMSIS-NN. The flash pack is loaded from a .bin file rather than linked from flash.  This is the fast, flash-free equivalent of the `moonshine_micro_tts` firmware + tts_speak.py: same bytes in, same PCM out, no board required. Text in, 16 kHz mono int16 PCM chunks out. Everything else -- G2P, duration rules, diphone/word unit selection, RVQ decode through the s16x8 TFLM graph, prosody shaping, and WORLD-lite vocoding -- happens behind this interface, driven by a single flash-resident data pack (g_neural_tts_pack, built by scripts/export_neural_tts_pack.py).  The synthesis pipeline mirrors the Phase A/B host reference (scripts/synth_diphone_world.py with the shipping flag set: cap 32, w_join 5, xfade 3, gain_eq, dur_mode=unit, f0_mode=unit_decl, prosody_shape, timbre_norm 0.3, f0_norm, prosody model), with these deliberate on-device simplifications: * word-unit continuity costs skip the log-envelope term (edge vectors are stored for diphones only), * diphone candidate pools are capped at 8 (the pack stores <= 6 usage-ranked candidates per type anyway; only class-fallback pools were ever larger), * long inputs are split into <= ~5 s chunks at silence (then word-gap) boundaries and synthesized sequentially, so RAM stays bounded.  Typical use (tts_service.cc): neural_tts::NeuralTts tts(cfg, arena, arena_size);   // once tts.Synthesize(\"hello world\", emit_fn, user);        // per utterance  The arena is only used inside Synthesize() calls; between calls it can be lent to other subsystems (VAD / STT), matching the app's phase- disjoint arena sharing.  ifndef NEURAL_TTS_NEURAL_TTS_H_", "id": "micro/neural-tts/include/neural_tts/neural_tts.h", "kind": "module", "label": "neural_tts.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "0d541180456f19dc", "symbol_count": 12, "symbols": [{"doc": "Wall-clock breakdown of the most recent Synthesize*/EstimateSamples* call (microseconds). Renders 61-control WORLD-lite frames -- f0 (Hz, 0 = unvoiced), benv[48] (sqrt-power spectral envelope at mel knots), bap[12] (aperiodicity at mel band centers) at 5 ms / 16 kHz -- to PCM. This is a single-precision port of WORLD's Synthesis() (mmorise/World, BSD-3-Clause): pitch-synchronous minimum-phase impulse responses plus shaped noise, overlap-added at phase-derived pulse locations. Differences from upstream WORLD:  * float32 + kiss_fftr everywhere (the M33 FPU is single-precision; double is softfloat and ~10x slower). * the band envelope / aperiodicity expansion (mel piecewise-linear to the 513-bin FFT grid, models/neural_tts/worldlite.py expand()) is fused in, so callers pass band controls, not full spectra. * unvoiced pulse rate is 200 Hz (one per 5 ms frame) instead of WORLD's 500 Hz default -- 2.5x fewer noise FFTs, no audible change (validated against pyworld on the host). * streaming output: overlap-add happens in a 2048-sample ring and finished samples are emitted as int16 chunks, so a full-utterance float PCM buffer is never held in RAM.  ifndef NEURAL_TTS_WORLDLITE_SYNTH_H_ define NEURAL_TTS_WORLDLITE_SYNTH_H_  include <cstdint>  include \"kiss_fftr.h\"", "id": "micro/neural-tts/include/neural_tts/worldlite_synth.h", "kind": "module", "label": "worldlite_synth.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "051eb9cf8f71a733", "symbol_count": 20, "symbols": [{"doc": "Per-frame controls in the deploy parameterization.", "kind": "struct", "line": 51, "name": "WorldFrame"}, {"kind": "struct", "line": 92, "name": "BinMap"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 57, "name": "WorldLiteSynth"}, {"doc": "Bytes kiss_fftr_alloc needs for one real-FFT plan (query with mem=nullptr).", "kind": "function", "line": 39, "name": "KissFftrPlanBytes", "signature": "inline size_t KissFftrPlanBytes(int nfft, int inverse_fft)"}, {"doc": "Forward + inverse plan storage for Synthesize() (typically ~21 KiB at nfft=1024).", "kind": "function", "line": 46, "name": "KissFftrPairBytes", "signature": "inline size_t KissFftrPairBytes(int nfft)"}, {"doc": "False if kissfft plan setup failed; classifier.  Single public header for the module. It exposes:  * Classifier -- a TFLM wrapper around the int8 mel-mode SpellingCNN. Run() takes fp32 log-mel features (from the feature-generation module) and returns dequantized fp32 logits.  * Argmax / SoftmaxProb -- small stateless helpers to turn logits into a prediction index + top-1 probability for logging.  The classifier is shape- and model-agnostic: the model bytes, arena, and the expected (n_mels, target_frames, n_classes) are all supplied by the caller, so the module carries no model or platform dependency beyond feature-generation and TFLM. A single Classifier instance must live for the whole run (the MicroInterpreter holds pointers into the arena handed to it).  ifndef STT_STT_H_ define STT_STT_H_  include <cstddef> include <cstdint>", "id": "micro/stt/include/stt/stt.h", "kind": "module", "label": "stt.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "1555f477ff683881", "symbol_count": 14, "symbols": [{"doc": "Quantization parameters at a model tensor boundary.", "kind": "struct", "line": 35, "name": "TensorQuant"}, {"kind": "struct", "line": 74, "name": "Impl"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 40, "name": "Classifier"}, {"doc": "Scratch for the fp32 log-mel features, carved from the arena's activation overlay (dead until Invoke()). Contract: produce features here, then call Run(feature_scratch()). The values do NOT survive Run().", "kind": "function", "line": 65, "name": "feature_scratch", "signature": "float* feature_scratch() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 66, "name": "input_quant", "signature": "TensorQuant input_quant() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 68, "name": "output_quant", "signature": "TensorQuant output_quant() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 69, "name": "n_classes", "signature": "int n_classes() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 70, "name": "input_count", "signature": "std::size_t input_count() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 71, "name": "arena_used_bytes", "signature": "std::size_t arena_used_bytes() const"}, {"doc": "Construct from the flatbuffer + a caller-owned tensor arena (which must outlive the Classifier). expected_* are sanity-checked against the model on a noisy halt -- no recovery path makes sense this early in boot. `profiler`, if non-null, is handed to the interpreter so per-op timings are recorded on every Invoke(); it must outlive the Classifier.", "kind": "function", "line": 47, "name": "Classifier", "signature": "Classifier(const unsigned char* model_data, unsigned int model_size, uint8_t* tensor_arena, std::size_t tensor_arena_size, int expected_n_mels, int expected_target_frames, int expected_n_classes, tfli"}, {"doc": "Run a single inference. `features` is the row-major (n_mels * target_frames) fp32 log-mel buffer; `logits_out` must hold n_classes() floats. We quantize into the int8 input, Invoke, dequantize the int8 output. `features` may safely point at feature_scratch().", "kind": "function", "line": 60, "name": "Run", "signature": "void Run(const float* features, float* logits_out) const;"}, {"doc": "Index of the largest logit. Ties go to the lowest index.", "kind": "function", "line": 90, "name": "Argmax", "signature": "int Argmax(const float* logits, int n_logits);"}, {"doc": "Stable-softmax probability of `index` (subtracts max(logits) before exp()).", "kind": "function", "line": 93, "name": "SoftmaxProb", "signature": "float SoftmaxProb(const float* logits, int n_logits, int index);"}, {"kind": "macro", "line": 19, "name": "STT_STT_H_", "signature": "#define STT_STT_H_"}]}, {"id": "micro/stt/scripts/desktop_parity.py", "kind": "module", "label": "desktop_parity.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "8e6c8148d5c320e6", "symbol_count": 5, "symbols": [{"doc": "Load whichever metadata sidecar sits next to the model.\n\nAccepts both the current ``spelling_cnn_meta.json`` and the older\nmode-qualified ``spelling_cnn.mel_meta.json`` so this works against\nhistorical runs too. Missing dims are filled with the project's\nlong-standing LogMelSpectrogram defaults and can be overridden on the\nCLI.", "kind": "function", "line": 60, "name": "_resolve_meta", "signature": "def _resolve_meta(tflite)"}, {"doc": "Replicate the embedded int16 blob and the firmware's inverse.\n\n``generate_embedded_data._fp32_to_int16_pcm`` stores ``round(x*32767)``\n(saturated); ``main.cc`` reads it back as ``int16 * (1/32768)``. Doing\nboth here makes the fp32 waveform identical to what the board feeds its\nlog-mel front-end.", "kind": "function", "line": 76, "name": "_int16_roundtrip", "signature": "def _int16_roundtrip(samples)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 92, "name": "_softmax_prob", "signature": "def _softmax_prob(logits, idx)"}, {"doc": "Pull ``(exp, got)`` pairs from a pico_monitor.log per-clip table.", "kind": "function", "line": 98, "name": "_parse_device_log", "signature": "def _parse_device_log(path)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 111, "name": "main", "signature": "def main(argv)"}]}, {"id": "micro/stt/scripts/generate_embedded_data.py", "kind": "module", "label": "generate_embedded_data.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "93ac24fcd57bfad4", "symbol_count": 20, "symbols": [{"doc": "Traditional include-guard macro for a generated header stem (no ext).", "kind": "function", "line": 63, "name": "_include_guard", "signature": "def _include_guard(stem)"}, {"doc": "Return the checked-in SpellingCNN int8 model under moonshine-micro/models/.", "kind": "function", "line": 68, "name": "_resolve_int8_mel_tflite", "signature": "def _resolve_int8_mel_tflite(explicit)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 90, "name": "_meta_sidecar", "signature": "def _meta_sidecar(tflite)"}, {"doc": "Load the model's audio metadata, or die loudly if it's missing.\n\nHARD-FAIL design: the on-device log-mel front-end MUST exactly match\nthe front-end the model expects. Silently defaulting any of\nn_mels / target_frames / hop_length / n_fft to legacy values was a silent\ncorruption mode -- the C++ build would succeed and the firmware would halt\ninside TFLM AllocateTensors() with no visible error.", "kind": "function", "line": 103, "name": "_load_meta", "signature": "def _load_meta(tflite)"}, {"doc": "Render `data` as comma-separated 0x.. literals, wrapping every `width`.", "kind": "function", "line": 142, "name": "_format_byte_array", "signature": "def _format_byte_array(data, width)"}, {"doc": "Render signed int16 samples as comma-separated literals.", "kind": "function", "line": 151, "name": "_format_int16_array", "signature": "def _format_int16_array(samples, width)"}, {"doc": "Round a Python float (f64) to the nearest IEEE-754 float32 value.\n\nThe on-device tables are ``float`` arrays, so we bake exactly the\nfloat32 value the compiler will store. ``repr()`` of the result is\nthe shortest decimal that round-trips back to that float32, so the\nemitted literal is unambiguous.", "kind": "function", "line": 160, "name": "_f32", "signature": "def _f32(x)"}, {"doc": "Render floats as comma-separated C ``float`` literals (``...f``).", "kind": "function", "line": 171, "name": "_format_float32_array", "signature": "def _format_float32_array(vals, width)"}, {"doc": "Render ints as comma-separated literals (no width padding).", "kind": "function", "line": 180, "name": "_format_plain_int_array", "signature": "def _format_plain_int_array(vals, width)"}, {"doc": "Symmetric 16-bit quantization with saturation.\n\nMatches the inverse of `read_wav_mono`'s scaling (which divides\nint16 PCM by 32768). We multiply by 32767 (not 32768) so a sample of\n+1.0 maps to INT16_MAX rather than wrapping to -32768, and we clip\nout-of-range values explicitly because audio mastering occasionally\nproduces samples slightly above +1.0 in float-WAV captures.", "kind": "function", "line": 189, "name": "_fp32_to_int16_pcm", "signature": "def _fp32_to_int16_pcm(samples)"}, {"doc": "True when ``path`` looks n_samples), return int16 PCM.", "kind": "function", "line": 216, "name": "_load_clip", "signature": "def _load_clip(path, sample_rate, n_samples)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 228, "name": "_write_model_files", "signature": "def _write_model_files(out_dir, tflite)"}, {"doc": "Emit ``audio_config.h`` with the model's mel-front-end constants.\n\nGenerated from the model metadata sidecar so dimension changes propagate\ninto the firmware without hand-editing ``main.cc``. ``f_max`` is the Nyquist\nfrequency (sample_rate / 2).\n\n``n_fft`` MUST match the value baked into the model: the Slaney mel\nfilterbank is computed from the FFT freq bins, so a mismatch silently\ncorrupts predictions even if the rest of the audio config agrees.", "kind": "function", "line": 268, "name": "_write_audio_config_file", "signature": "def _write_audio_config_file(out_dir)"}, {"doc": "Emit ``mel_tables.{h,cc}``: the precomputed Hann window + CSR mel\nfilterbank, as ``const`` arrays the linker places in flash.\n\nThis lets the on-device ``LogMelSpectrogram`` SKIP all front-end\nconstruction work (the triangular Slaney filterbank, the periodic\nHann window) and instead point straight at these read-only tables.\nThe win + filterbank therefore cost ZERO RAM (they live in XIP\nflash) and ZERO boot-time trig/log -- the constructor just stores\nfour pointers.\n\nPARITY: the window and filterbank are computed by the SAME reference\nfunctions the desktop pipeline uses (``models.log_mel_pure``'s\n``hann_window`` and ``make_mel_filterbank``), which the on-device\nC++ ``HannWindowPeriodic`` / ``MakeMelFilterbank`` were written to\nmirror. Values are baked as exact float32 literals (see ``_f32``).\nThe CSR sparsity pattern (which (m, k) entries are nonzero) matches\n``PureLogMelSpectrogram._apply_mel``'s ``fb_row[k] != 0.0`` filter,\nso the device sums exactly the same terms as the reference.", "kind": "function", "line": 327, "name": "_write_mel_tables_file", "signature": "def _write_mel_tables_file(out_dir)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 465, "name": "_write_classes_files", "signature": "def _write_classes_files(out_dir, classes)"}, {"doc": "Write one ``int16`` array per clip plus a small descriptor table.\n\nEach clip is emitted as a file-scope static array so the linker can\nplace individual blobs anywhere in flash. The descriptor table\ncarries label index, source path, and the array pointer + length so\nmain.cc can iterate without per-clip switch statements.\n\n``decoded`` items are ``(label_idx, label, source_display, samples)``\nwhere ``samples`` is already int16 PCM (decoded from a local wav or a\nHub clip) so this formatter is source-agnostic.", "kind": "function", "line": 501, "name": "_write_clips_files", "signature": "def _write_clips_files(out_dir, decoded, sample_rate, n_samples)"}, {"doc": "Pick a deterministic per-class subset (alphabetical by filename).", "kind": "function", "line": 586, "name": "_pick_clips", "signature": "def _pick_clips(wavs_roots, classes, clips_per_class, max_classes)"}, {"doc": "Pick a deterministic per-class subset from packed HF speech shards.\n\nEach selected clip's wav bytes are staged to a temp file and decoded with\nthe SAME stdlib ``read_wav_mono`` path the local branch uses, so the\nembedded int16 PCM is byte-for-byte identical regardless of source.\nReturns ``(label_idx, label, source_display, int16_samples)`` records.", "kind": "function", "line": 617, "name": "_pick_clips_hub", "signature": "def _pick_clips_hub(repo_id, configs, classes, clips_per_class, max_classes, sample_rate, n_samples, cache_dir)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 680, "name": "main", "signature": "def main(argv)"}]}, {"doc": "TFLM-based on-device classifier. See classifier.h for the contract. handful of TFLM platform hooks that the modules and the micro_test.h harness reference: the MicroPrintf logging family and tflite::InitializeTarget().  The vendored pico-tflmicro provides these for the RP2350 via system_setup.cpp / debug_log.cpp, both of which call into the Pico SDK and therefore cannot be compiled on the host. For the pure-logic unit tests (feature-generation, the VAD segmenter, the STT predictor, the TTS G2P) we don't need the interpreter at all -- only logging and a no-op init -- so this tiny shim lets those tests build and run on a laptop with a normal compiler.  Interpreter-level tests (real MicroInterpreter inference) are built for the RP2350 target instead, where the full pico-tflmicro library is available.  include <cstdarg> include <cstddef> include <cstdio>", "id": "micro/test-support/host/tflm_host_stub.cc", "kind": "module", "label": "tflm_host_stub.cc", "language": "cc", "sha256": "b730d0195934bc52", "symbol_count": 10, "symbols": [{"doc": "include <cstdarg> include <cstddef> include <cstdio>", "kind": "function", "line": 18, "name": "MicroPrintf", "signature": "void MicroPrintf(const char* format, ...)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 26, "name": "VMicroPrintf", "signature": "void VMicroPrintf(const char* format, va_list args)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 31, "name": "MicroSnprintf", "signature": "int MicroSnprintf(char* buffer, size_t buf_size, const char* format, ...)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 39, "name": "MicroVsnprintf", "signature": "int MicroVsnprintf(char* buffer, size_t buf_size, const char* format,\n                   va_list ..."}, {"kind": "function", "line": 46, "name": "InitializeTarget", "signature": "void InitializeTarget()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 21, "name": "va_start", "signature": "va_start(args, format);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 22, "name": "vfprintf", "signature": "vfprintf(stderr, format, args);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 23, "name": "va_end", "signature": "va_end(args);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 24, "name": "fputc", "signature": "fputc('\\n', stderr);"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 42, "name": "vsnprintf", "signature": "return vsnprintf(buffer, buf_size, format, vlist);"}]}, {"doc": "Run a TFLM micro_test.h binary and translate its output into an exit code.  micro_test.h wraps the suite in `while (true) { ... }` (it is designed to run forever on an embedded target and stream results over serial). On the host we read until the first pass/fail banner, then quit -- closing the pipe sends the looping binary a SIGPIPE so it terminates. Exit 0 iff all tests passed.", "id": "micro/test-support/run_micro_test.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "run_micro_test.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "0895122590440946", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"doc": "vad -- on-device voice activity detection.  Single public header for the module. It exposes the two halves of the VAD:  * Vad            -- a TFLM wrapper around the int8 TinyVadCNN. Given a normalised (n_mels x window_frames) log-mel window it returns ONE speech probability in [0, 1]. One call per ~32 ms streaming hop.  * VadSegmenter   -- a heap-free moving-average smoother + 1 s clip extractor. It turns the per-frame probabilities into speech-segment boundaries (absolute sample indices on the input stream) without storing any audio.  The streaming log-mel front-end that feeds Vad lives in the feature-generation module (MelStreamer); compose them in your application (see examples/rp2350's audio path). The VAD model is shape-agnostic: the model bytes, arena, and (n_mels, window_frames) are all supplied by the caller, so the module carries no model or platform dependency beyond feature-generation and TFLM.  ifndef VAD_VAD_H_ define VAD_VAD_H_  include <cstddef> include <cstdint>", "id": "micro/vad/include/vad/vad.h", "kind": "module", "label": "vad.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "db4b2cf059c21400", "symbol_count": 23, "symbols": [{"kind": "struct", "line": 38, "name": "VadTensorQuant"}, {"kind": "struct", "line": 72, "name": "Impl"}, {"kind": "enum", "line": 85, "name": "VadEvent"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 43, "name": "Vad"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 85, "name": "VadEvent"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 96, "name": "VadSegmenter"}, {"doc": "Scratch for the fp32 log-mel window, borrowed from the arena overlay (dead until Invoke()). Contract: produce features here, then Predict(it).", "kind": "function", "line": 64, "name": "feature_scratch", "signature": "float* feature_scratch() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 65, "name": "input_quant", "signature": "VadTensorQuant input_quant() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 67, "name": "output_quant", "signature": "VadTensorQuant output_quant() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 68, "name": "input_count", "signature": "std::size_t input_count() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 69, "name": "arena_used_bytes", "signature": "std::size_t arena_used_bytes() const"}, {"doc": "Boundaries (absolute sample indices) of the most-recent segment.", "kind": "function", "line": 113, "name": "segment_start_sample", "signature": "std::size_t segment_start_sample() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 114, "name": "segment_end_sample", "signature": "std::size_t segment_end_sample() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 115, "name": "samples_processed", "signature": "std::size_t samples_processed() const"}, {"doc": "Construct from the flatbuffer + a caller-owned tensor arena (which must outlive the Vad). expected_* are sanity-checked against the model on a noisy halt. Because the VAD never Invoke()s at the same time as the STT classifier, it can share the STT tensor arena.", "kind": "function", "line": 49, "name": "Vad", "signature": "Vad(const unsigned char* model_data, unsigned int model_size, uint8_t* tensor_arena, std::size_t tensor_arena_size, int expected_n_mels, int expected_window_frames, tflite::MicroProfilerInterface* pro"}, {"doc": "Run one inference on a (n_mels * window_frames) row-major fp32 log-mel window; returns the speech probability in [0, 1] (sigmoid of the dequantized logit). `features` may point at feature_scratch().", "kind": "function", "line": 60, "name": "Predict", "signature": "float Predict(const float* features) const;"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 97, "name": "VadSegmenter", "signature": "public: VadSegmenter(float threshold, int window_frames, int hop, std::size_t look_behind_samples, std::size_t max_segment_samples);"}, {"doc": "Reset all state to begin a fresh stream.", "kind": "function", "line": 103, "name": "Start", "signature": "void Start();"}, {"doc": "Advance one frame (== hop samples) given the model's RAW (un-smoothed) speech probability. Returns the transition that occurred, if any.", "kind": "function", "line": 107, "name": "ProcessFrame", "signature": "VadEvent ProcessFrame(float raw_probability);"}, {"doc": "Flush a trailing open segment at end-of-stream.", "kind": "function", "line": 110, "name": "Finish", "signature": "VadEvent Finish();"}, {"doc": "Front-aligned pad/truncate of src[start, end) into out[0, clip_len): take from the segment start, zero-pad the tail. `out` must hold clip_len floats.", "kind": "function", "line": 135, "name": "ExtractClipFrontAligned", "signature": "void ExtractClipFrontAligned(const float* src, std::size_t src_len, std::size_t start, std::size_t end, float* out, std::size_t clip_len);"}, {"doc": "Power-weighted centroid sample index over buf[start, end): round( sum(i * buf[i]^2) / sum(buf[i]^2) ). Used to re-centre the captured clip on the spoken word's energy instead of the noisy VAD segment_start -- this closes most of the streaming-VAD accuracy gap in host simulation (see scripts/test_streaming_vad.py --align-sweep).", "kind": "function", "line": 145, "name": "EnergyCentroidIndex", "signature": "std::size_t EnergyCentroidIndex(const int16_t* buf, std::size_t start, std::size_t end);"}, {"kind": "macro", "line": 23, "name": "VAD_VAD_H_", "signature": "#define VAD_VAD_H_"}]}, {"id": "micro/vad/scripts/generate_vad_embedded_data.py", "kind": "module", "label": "generate_vad_embedded_data.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "ae51047c9401923e", "symbol_count": 6, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 66, "name": "_smooth_window_frames", "signature": "def _smooth_window_frames()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 72, "name": "_write_vad_config", "signature": "def _write_vad_config(out_dir)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 117, "name": "_write_vad_mel_tables", "signature": "def _write_vad_mel_tables(out_dir)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 190, "name": "_write_vad_model", "signature": "def _write_vad_model(out_dir, tflite)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 224, "name": "_auto_tflite", "signature": "def _auto_tflite()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 229, "name": "main", "signature": "def main(argv)"}]}, {"doc": "TFLM-based on-device VAD inference. "python/src/moonshine_voice/alphanumeric_listener.py", "kind": "module", "label": "alphanumeric_listener.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "bd38b31c8883cd64", "symbol_count": 31, "symbols": [{"kind": "class", "line": 40, "name": "AlphanumericEventType", "signature": "class AlphanumericEventType(Enum)"}, {"doc": "Event delivered to the callback each time something happens.\n\nAttributes\n----------\ntype:\n    The kind of event (CHARACTER, UNDO, CLEAR, or STOPPED).\ncharacter:\n    The resolved character for CHARACTER events, or the removed\n    character for UNDO events. ``None`` for CLEAR / STOPPED.\ntext:\n    The full assembled string *after* this event has been applied.", "kind": "class", "line": 49, "name": "AlphanumericEvent", "signature": "class AlphanumericEvent"}, {"doc": "Pure classification result produced by :class:`AlphanumericMatcher`.\n\nHas a ``type`` (one of :class:`AlphanumericEventType`, with ``NONE``\nmeaning \"unrecognized\") and an optional resolved ``character``.", "kind": "class", "line": 69, "name": "AlphanumericMatch", "signature": "class AlphanumericMatch"}, {"doc": "Return a TTS-friendly phrase for a single character.\n\n* Letters use their spelling-alphabet sounds – ``\"h\"`` → ``\"haitch\"``,\n  ``\"w\"`` → ``\"double you\"``.\n* Upper-case letters are prefixed with ``\"capital \"`` –\n  ``\"H\"`` → ``\"capital haitch\"``.\n* Digits become their word form – ``\"1\"`` → ``\"one\"``.\n* Common symbols use their spoken name – ``\"#\"`` → ``\"hash\"``,\n  ``\"@\"`` → ``\"at sign\"``, ``\" \"`` → ``\"space\"``.\n* Anything else (unknown char, empty string, multi-char input) is\n  returned unchanged so callers never lose information silently.", "kind": "method", "line": 306, "name": "spoken_form", "signature": "def spoken_form(char)"}, {"doc": "Return *text* lower-cased with quotes/punctuation removed.\n\nCharacters in :data:`_NORMALIZE_DROP_CHARS` are deleted, the result is\nlower-cased, and internal runs of whitespace are collapsed to a single\nspace.  Used on both inbound STT text and the vocabulary keys so\nmatching is robust to noisy punctuation while still recognising\nmulti-word phrases like ``\"upper case\"``.", "kind": "method", "line": 355, "name": "_normalize", "signature": "def _normalize(text)"}, {"doc": "Merge all character vocabularies into a single lookup table.", "kind": "method", "line": 370, "name": "_build_lookup", "signature": "def _build_lookup()"}, {"doc": "Parse English number words in the range 10 – 1 000.\n\nHandles forms like:\n  - \"ten\" .. \"nineteen\"\n  - \"twenty\" .. \"ninety nine\" (with or without hyphen)\n  - \"one hundred\" .. \"nine hundred and ninety nine\"\n  - \"a hundred\", \"a thousand\", \"one thousand\"\n\nReturns ``None`` when *text* is not a recognisable number phrase or\nis in the range 0 – 9 (those are handled by the single-digit lookup).", "kind": "method", "line": 424, "name": "_parse_number_words", "signature": "def _parse_number_words(text)"}, {"doc": "Stateless classifier for spelled letter / digit / command utterances.\n\nExposes the \"does this utterance match?\" half of the alphanumeric\nvocabulary as a pure function, without any of the listener or\nbuffer-management machinery.  This is useful for dialog flows that\nwant to reuse the same vocabulary for ``ask(mode=SPELLED)`` or\n``ask(mode=DIGITS)`` prompts without pulling in the whole event\nlistener.\n\nThe same recognition rules apply as for :class:`AlphanumericListener`:\nletters, digits, number words 10-1000, upper-case modifiers, special\ncharacters, and the undo / clear / stop command vocabularies.\n\nParameters\n----------\ncustom_words:\n    Optional dict mapping spoken forms to output characters.  Takes\n    highest priority and overrides built-in mappings.\naccept_letters:\n    If ``False``, utterances that resolve to an alphabetic character\n    are reported as ``NONE`` (useful for digit-only modes).\naccept_digits:\n    If ``False``, utterances that resolve to a digit character are\n    reported as ``NONE`` (useful for letter-only modes).\naccept_specials:\n    If ``False``, utterances that resolve to a special character\n    (``@``, ``#``, …) are reported as ``NONE``.", "kind": "class", "line": 512, "name": "AlphanumericMatcher", "signature": "class AlphanumericMatcher"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 716, "name": "letters_only_matcher", "signature": "def letters_only_matcher()"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 720, "name": "digits_only_matcher", "signature": "def digits_only_matcher()"}, {"doc": "Listens for single-character dictation and assembles the result.\n\nThis is a callable listener — pass it directly to\n``transcriber.add_listener()`` or ``stream.add_listener()``.  It\nreceives raw :class:`TranscriptEvent` objects and internally filters\nfor the events it cares about.  All utterance-level recognition is\ndelegated to :class:`AlphanumericMatcher`; this class only adds the\nlistener plumbing (buffer, undo/clear/stop state, event dispatch).\n\nA single *callback* is invoked every time something meaningful\nhappens.  The callback receives an :class:`AlphanumericEvent` whose\n``type`` field describes what occurred:\n\n* ``CHARACTER`` — a letter, digit, or special character was recognised.\n* ``UNDO``      — the last character was removed.\n* ``CLEAR``     — the buffer was wiped.\n* ``STOPPED``   — the user said \"stop\" / \"done\" / \"finish\" / etc.\n\nSee :class:`AlphanumericMatcher` for the full vocabulary.\n\nParameters\n----------\ncallback:\n    Called on every character, undo, clear, or stop event.\n    Signature: ``(event: AlphanumericEvent) -> None``.\nuse_line_completed:\n    If ``True`` (default), characters are committed on\n    ``LineCompleted`` events (high confidence).  If ``False``,\n    characters are committed on ``LineTextChanged`` for lower\n    latency.\ncustom_words:\n    Optional dict mapping spoken forms to output characters.\n    Takes highest priority and overrides built-in mappings.\nmatcher:\n    Optional pre-built :class:`AlphanumericMatcher`.  When provided,\n    ``custom_words`` is ignored and the matcher is used as-is.\ntts:\n    Optional text-to-speech backend.  When provided:\n\n    * Each ``CHARACTER`` event triggers a ``tts.say(phrase)`` call\n      where ``phrase`` is the output of :func:`spoken_form` (e.g.\n      ``\"haitch\"`` for ``\"h\"``, ``\"capital ay\"`` for ``\"A\"``,\n      ``\"one\"`` for ``\"1\"``, ``\"hash\"`` for ``\"#\"``).\n    * Each utterance the matcher *doesn't* recognise triggers a\n      ``tts.play_error()`` call (a short two-tone beep), so the\n      user hears audible feedback that their last word was\n      ignored instead of waiting in silence.\n\n    The backend needs to expose ``say(text: str) -> None`` for the\n    per-character repeat-back; ``play_error()`` is called only if\n    the backend actually defines it (so simple stubs stay usable).\n    Exceptions from either call are swallowed (and logged under\n    ``debug=True``) so a flaky TTS can't break the listener.\ndebug:\n    If ``True``, unrecognised utterances and TTS errors are logged\n    to stderr.\n\nNotes\n-----\nThe optional spelling-CNN fusion path used to live here as a\nPython ``SpellingPredictor`` + ``FusionStrategy`` smart-router.\nThat logic now ships in the C++ transcriber: build the\n:class:`Transcriber` with ``spelling_model_path=…`` and pass\n``MOONSHINE_FLAG_SPELLING_MODE`` to your ``transcribe_*`` /\n``update_transcription`` calls; this listener will then see\nalready-resolved single-character ``line.text`` values for the\nmatched utterances.", "kind": "class", "line": 738, "name": "AlphanumericListener", "signature": "class AlphanumericListener"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 80, "name": "is_character", "signature": "def is_character(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 84, "name": "is_terminator", "signature": "def is_terminator(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 88, "name": "is_recognized", "signature": "def is_recognized(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 542, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self)"}, {"doc": "Classify a single utterance into an :class:`AlphanumericMatch`.", "kind": "method", "line": 570, "name": "classify", "signature": "def classify(self, raw_text)"}, {"doc": "Classify a potentially multi-token utterance.\n\nFirst tries to classify the utterance as a whole; if that returns\n``NONE`` and the utterance contains multiple tokens, falls back to\nclassifying each token individually (so ``\"h o m e\"`` resolves to\nfour ``CHARACTER`` events).  The returned list preserves order and\nstops after the first ``STOPPED`` match.", "kind": "method", "line": 606, "name": "classify_sequence", "signature": "def classify_sequence(self, raw_text)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 637, "name": "_resolve", "signature": "def _resolve(self, text)"}, {"doc": "Recognise speller patterns like ``\"A for Alpha\"`` / ``\"B as in Boy\"``.\n\nThe text is split on a small set of connector phrases (``\"for\"``,\n``\"as in\"``, ``\"is for\"``, ``\"like\"``).  We accept the utterance\nwhen:\n\n* The left side resolves through :attr:`_lookup` to a single\n  alphabetic character -- so ``\"a\"``, ``\"bee\"``, ``\"alpha\"``,\n  ``\"whiskey\"`` are all valid spellers, but ``\"one\"`` (digit) or\n  ``\"hash\"`` (special) are not.\n* The right side is a single word whose first character matches\n  the resolved letter (case-insensitive).  This covers both the\n  NATO codewords (``\"A for Alpha\"``) and free-form memory aids\n  (``\"B as in Boy\"``, ``\"M for Mary\"``) without us having to\n  enumerate every English word.\n\nWithout this pattern handler the matcher's word-by-word fallback\nwould tokenise ``\"A for Alpha\"`` into ``a`` + ``4`` + ``a``,\nbecause ``\"for\"`` is a registered homophone of ``\"four\"`` in the\ndigit vocabulary -- so we have to short-circuit the whole-utterance\nmatch here.\n\nConnectors are checked most-specific-first so ``\"a is for alpha\"``\nsplits on ``\"is for\"`` before the bare ``\"for\"`` substring inside\nit has a chance to match.  When a connector splits the text but\nthe halves don't validate (e.g. ``\"a for bravo\"``) we ``continue``\nto try the next connector instead of returning, so an unrelated\nsubstring collision can't poison a later valid match.", "kind": "method", "line": 652, "name": "_resolve_spelled_letter", "signature": "def _resolve_spelled_letter(self, text)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 705, "name": "_char_accepted", "signature": "def _char_accepted(self, char)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 808, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, callback)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 829, "name": "__call__", "signature": "def __call__(self, event)"}, {"doc": "The currently assembled text.", "kind": "method", "line": 840, "name": "text", "signature": "def text(self)"}, {"doc": "Whether a stop command has been received.", "kind": "method", "line": 845, "name": "stopped", "signature": "def stopped(self)"}, {"doc": "The underlying :class:`AlphanumericMatcher`.", "kind": "method", "line": 850, "name": "matcher", "signature": "def matcher(self)"}, {"doc": "Programmatically clear the buffer.", "kind": "method", "line": 854, "name": "clear", "signature": "def clear(self)"}, {"doc": "Remove and return the last character, or ``None`` if empty.", "kind": "method", "line": 865, "name": "undo", "signature": "def undo(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 879, "name": "_process_utterance", "signature": "def _process_utterance(self, line)"}, {"doc": "Speak the TTS phrase for ``char`` if a TTS backend is wired.", "kind": "method", "line": 941, "name": "_speak_character", "signature": "def _speak_character(self, char)"}, {"doc": "Ask the TTS backend to play its error beep, if it supports one.\n\nCalled from the unrecognised-utterance branch so the user hears\na short audible cue that their last word was ignored.
