Defaults to the TSV packaged with\n    :mod:`moonshine_voice`.  If the file is missing the cache is\n    simply empty – behaviour is then governed entirely by\n    ``fallback``.\nfallback:\n    Optional embedding backend consulted on cache misses.  If\n    ``None``, :meth:`calculate_embedding` raises on misses.\nexpected_model_name / expected_model_variant:\n    Optional strings.  When the TSV metadata does not match these,\n    the cache is *disabled* (wiped in-memory and a warning is logged\n    to stderr) so you never accidentally mix embeddings from\n    different models. Raises ``KeyError`` if neither\nyields a result.", "kind": "method", "line": 179, "name": "calculate_embedding", "signature": "def calculate_embedding(self, sentence)"}, {"doc": "Return the cosine similarity between two embedding vectors.\n\nThe cache itself does not implement similarity scoring – it\ndelegates to the configured ``fallback`` backend (typically an\n:class:`~moonshine_voice.IntentRecognizer`) so the underlying\nnative ``moonshine_calculate_embedding_distance`` C function is\nused.  Raises :class:`RuntimeError` when no fallback is\nconfigured.", "kind": "method", "line": 195, "name": "distance", "signature": "def distance(self, embedding_a, embedding_b)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 218, "name": "_load", "signature": "def _load(self, path)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 238, "name": "_parse_meta", "signature": "def _parse_meta(self, s)"}, {"doc": "Normalize a phrase for lookup.\n\nWe store and look up phrases in a case-folded, whitespace-stripped\nform so the cache is forgiving about minor casing differences in\nthe caller's registration.", "kind": "method", "line": 245, "name": "_normalize", "signature": "def _normalize(s)"}]}, {"id": "python/src/moonshine_voice/cli.py", "kind": "module", "label": "cli.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "f3a72dcda7b42dd7", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 50, "name": "_package_version", "signature": "def _package_version()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 68, "name": "_usage", "signature": "def _usage()"}, {"doc": "Dispatch to a subcommand. Returns a process exit code.", "kind": "function", "line": 91, "name": "main", "signature": "def main(argv)"}]}, {"id": "python/src/moonshine_voice/dialog_flow.py", "kind": "module", "label": "dialog_flow.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "fe4770121a0dd101", "symbol_count": 94, "symbols": [{"doc": "Base class for values a flow function may yield to the runner.", "kind": "class", "line": 97, "name": "Prompt", "signature": "class Prompt"}, {"doc": "Speak ``text`` and resume the generator once playback has finished.", "kind": "class", "line": 102, "name": "Say", "signature": "class Say(Prompt)"}, {"doc": "Speak ``prompt`` and resume with the user's next utterance as a string.", "kind": "class", "line": 110, "name": "Ask", "signature": "class Ask(Prompt)"}, {"doc": "Speak ``prompt`` and resume with a bool (yes / no).", "kind": "class", "line": 147, "name": "Confirm", "signature": "class Confirm(Prompt)"}, {"doc": "Speak ``prompt`` and resume with the key of the matched option.\n\n``options`` maps option keys to canonical phrases.  Matching is done\nagainst the union of the key and its phrases, using the intent\nrecognizer when available and falling back to substring matching.", "kind": "class", "line": 166, "name": "Choose", "signature": "class Choose(Prompt)"}, {"doc": "Base class for dialog-flow exceptions.", "kind": "class", "line": 187, "name": "DialogError", "signature": "class DialogError(Exception)"}, {"doc": "Raised into / from a flow to abandon it entirely.", "kind": "class", "line": 191, "name": "DialogCancelled", "signature": "class DialogCancelled(DialogError)"}, {"doc": "Raised into / from a flow to restart it from the beginning.", "kind": "class", "line": 195, "name": "DialogRestart", "signature": "class DialogRestart(DialogError)"}, {"doc": "No utterance was received within the prompt's retry budget.", "kind": "class", "line": 199, "name": "NoInputError", "signature": "class NoInputError(DialogError)"}, {"doc": "Received an utterance but could not interpret it for this prompt.", "kind": "class", "line": 203, "name": "NoMatchError", "signature": "class NoMatchError(DialogError)"}, {"doc": "Minimal interface the phrase matcher needs from an embedding source.\n\n:class:`moonshine_voice.IntentRecognizer` satisfies this protocol via\nits :meth:`calculate_embedding` and :meth:`distance` methods – the\nlatter is a thin wrapper around the native\n``moonshine_calculate_embedding_distance`` C API so scoring happens\nin C rather than Python.", "kind": "class", "line": 212, "name": "EmbeddingBackend", "signature": "class EmbeddingBackend(Protocol)"}, {"doc": "Match an utterance to one of several key→phrases groups via embeddings.\n\nThis is a tiny wrapper around an :class:`EmbeddingBackend` (typically\nan :class:`IntentRecognizer`).  At construction time, the backend is\nused to compute an embedding for every phrase in every group; at\nmatch time, the utterance is embedded once and compared against\nevery phrase using cosine similarity.  The key of the best-scoring\nphrase (above ``threshold``) is returned, or *None* if nothing\nclears the threshold.\n\nUse this to replace string / substring matching on user utterances\nwith fuzzy, semantics-aware matching.\n\nExample::\n\n    yes_no = PhraseMatcher(\n        intent_recognizer,\n        {\"yes\": [\"yes\", \"sure\", \"please\"],\n         \"no\":  [\"no\", \"nope\", \"cancel\"]},\n        threshold=0.6,\n    )\n    assert yes_no.match(\"please go ahead\") == \"yes\"\n    assert yes_no.match(\"don't do that\")    == \"no\"", "kind": "class", "line": 229, "name": "PhraseMatcher", "signature": "class PhraseMatcher"}, {"doc": "Context object handed to a flow as its first argument.\n\nEach method returns a :class:`Prompt` that the flow yields; the runner\ncarries out the prompt and sends the result (if any) back into the\ngenerator.  ``Dialog`` itself performs no I/O, which keeps flows easy\nto unit-test: pass a ``Dialog`` to the flow, iterate the generator, and\ndrive it with ``.send()``.", "kind": "class", "line": 335, "name": "Dialog", "signature": "class Dialog"}, {"doc": "In-progress spelled / digit input buffered across utterances.", "kind": "class", "line": 432, "name": "_AlphaSession", "signature": "class _AlphaSession"}, {"doc": "Per-session state for a running flow.", "kind": "class", "line": 440, "name": "_ActiveFlow", "signature": "class _ActiveFlow"}, {"doc": "Runner that drives generator-based conversational flows.\n\nRegister flow functions against trigger phrases; completed transcript\nlines are routed either to the configured intent recognizer (when no\nflow is active) or to the currently suspended generator (when one is).\n\nThe runner is synchronous: when a flow yields a :class:`Say`, the\nrunner speaks and blocks until the utterance has been played, then\nresumes the generator.  When a flow yields an input-expecting prompt\n(:class:`Ask` / :class:`Confirm` / :class:`Choose`), the runner speaks\nthe prompt and returns control to the caller; the next completed\ntranscript line resumes the generator.\n\nArgs:\n    tts: Optional :class:`TextToSpeech` used to speak prompts.  If\n        set, prompts are spoken via ``tts.say(text)`` and the runner\n        blocks on ``tts.wait()`` before advancing the flow.\n    intent_recognizer: Optional :class:`IntentRecognizer` used for\n        matching trigger phrases to registered flows and for routing\n        utterances when no flow is active.  When omitted, trigger\n        matching falls back to case-insensitive substring matching.\n    transcriber: Reserved for future per-prompt biasing hooks.\n    speak_fn: Optional callable ``(text) -> None`` that speaks the text\n        and blocks until playback finishes.  Overrides ``tts``.  Useful\n        for tests and alternative TTS backends.\n    mute_fn: Optional callable ``(should_mute: bool) -> None`` invoked\n        before and after each spoken prompt so callers can silence the\n        microphone while the assistant is talking.\n    spell_feedback: If ``True`` (default), every character recognised\n        during a ``SPELLED`` / ``DIGITS`` prompt is spoken back to\n        the user using :func:`spoken_form` (``\"haitch\"`` for\n        ``\"h\"``, ``\"capital ay\"`` for ``\"A\"``, ``\"hash\"`` for\n        ``\"#\"``, etc.), and \"delete\" / \"backspace\" / \"undo\" /\n        \"scratch that\" commands are echoed as\n        ``\"deleting <character>\"`` so the user hears confirmation\n        that the right letter came off the end of the buffer.\n        Matches the behaviour of ``AlphanumericListener(tts=…)``\n        but routes through this runner's own\n        ``speak_fn``/``tts`` so the same mic-mute and logging\n        apply.  Pass ``spell_feedback=False`` to silence the\n        character-by-character echo (e.g. when no TTS is wired\n        up and audible output would just be log spam).\n    spelling_mode_fn: Optional callable\n        ``(active: bool) -> None`` invoked whenever the runner\n        enters or leaves a ``SPELLED`` / ``DIGITS`` prompt.  Wire\n        this to the underlying transcriber's\n        ``set_transcribe_flags`` to flip\n        ``MOONSHINE_FLAG_SPELLING_MODE`` on only while spelled\n        input is expected, so the C++ spelling-CNN fusion path is\n        used for password / code / digit dictation but doesn't\n        perturb free-form recognition or trigger-phrase matching.\n        Pairs with constructing the transcriber with a\n        ``spelling_model_path``; when no model is loaded the flag\n        is a no-op so leaving this ``None`` is also fine.\n    log_io: If ``True``, every utterance the runner receives from\n        the STT and every prompt it asks the TTS to speak is\n        logged to stderr in a clean ``user: …`` / ``assistant: …``\n        format.  Distinct from ``debug``: ``log_io`` is the\n        user-facing dialogue transcript (just inputs and\n        outputs), while ``debug`` is the verbose internal\n        stage-transition trace with timings.  Off by default so\n        existing callers that already format their own\n        transcript via ``speak_fn`` or a transcript listener\n        don't end up with duplicate lines; turn it on for a\n        quick inline trace when you don't care to wire up your\n        own logging.\n    ignore_stt_during_tts: If ``True`` (default), every utterance\n        that arrives while the runner is mid-prompt (i.e. the\n        TTS is actively speaking) is dropped before it can\n        advance the flow, match a global trigger, or fall\n        through to the intent recognizer.  This is a software\n        guard on top of the optional hardware ``mute_fn`` —\n        ``mute_fn`` minimises self-capture but on devices with\n        weak echo cancellation the STT can still latch onto\n        in-flight audio captured just before the mute, or onto\n        speaker bleed that the cancellation didn't fully\n        suppress.  Disable (``False``) only when you have\n        reliable echo cancellation *and* want barge-in: callers\n        still get the utterance via the regular\n        ``TranscriptEventListener`` path.\n    success_beep_fn: Optional callable ``() -> None`` invoked the\n        moment a completed transcript line is recognized — i.e.\n        it matched a trigger phrase or was successfully\n        interpreted as the answer to an active prompt — and\n        *before* any TTS response begins.  Gives the user a\n        short audible cue that \"I heard you and understood\"\n        before the assistant starts replying.  When omitted,\n        falls back to ``tts.play_success()`` if the configured\n        ``tts`` exposes one (e.g. the bundled\n        :class:`TextToSpeech`); pass any callable to override\n        (e.g. play a custom WAV) or ``lambda: None`` to\n        silence.\n    error_beep_fn: Optional callable ``() -> None`` invoked when\n        a completed transcript line *isn't* recognized — no\n        trigger matched, no active flow could interpret it as\n        an answer, and no global handler took it.  Pairs with\n        ``success_beep_fn`` so misrecognitions don't end in\n        silence: the user hears a distinct \"didn't get that\"\n        cue immediately, and the runner then reprompts /\n        abandons / forwards to the intent recognizer as before.\n        Same fallback as ``success_beep_fn`` — auto-wired to\n        ``tts.play_error()`` when available.", "kind": "class", "line": 453, "name": "DialogFlow", "signature": "class DialogFlow(TranscriptEventListener)"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 1619, "name": "_Reprompt", "signature": "class _Reprompt(Exception)"}, {"kind": "class", also iterates token-by-token.\n\nA ``str`` so ``f\"I heard: {spell_out(password)}\"`` interpolates as\nthe natural joined phrase (``\"ess ee ay bee\"``), but with\n``__iter__`` overridden to yield ``[\"ess\", \"ee\", \"ay\", \"bee\"]``.\nThat keeps backwards-compat with the older list-returning\n:func:`spell_out` API: a caller that wrote\n``\" \".join(spell_out(password))`` still gets the joined phrase\nback instead of the character-by-character ``\"e s s   e e   a y\nb e e\"`` you'd get from plain ``str`` iteration.", "kind": "class", "line": 1635, "name": "_SpelledPhrase", "signature": "class _SpelledPhrase(str)"}, {"doc": "Return ``s`` as a TTS-friendly spoken-form phrase.\n\nEach character is rendered as a phrase the TTS engine can pronounce\nunambiguously (letters use spelling-alphabet sounds like ``\"haitch\"``\nfor ``\"h\"``, upper-case letters are prefixed with ``\"capital \"``,\ndigits become word form, common symbols use their spoken name) and\nthe per-character phrases are joined with a single space.  The\nreturn value is a ``str`` subclass (:class:`_SpelledPhrase`) so it\ndrops cleanly into both an ``f\"I heard: {spell_out(password)}\"``\ninterpolation *and* a ``\" \".join(spell_out(password))`` call —\nboth produce the same joined phrase.  The per-character mapping\nlives in :func:`spoken_form` in ``alphanumeric_listener.py`` so\nthe :class:`AlphanumericListener`'s TTS repeat-back and this\nfunction can't drift apart.\n\n``spell_out(\"Hi#1\")`` renders as ``\"capital haitch eye hash\none\"`` (and iterates as\n``[\"capital\", \"haitch\", \"eye\", \"hash\", \"one\"]``).  Empty strings\nproduce ``\"\"``.  This is for *speaking* strings back at the user,\nnot for matching their input (that's\n:class:`AlphanumericMatcher`'s job); callers that need the\nstrict per-character list (e.g. for custom pacing between\ntokens) can use ``[spoken_form(c) for c in s]`` directly.", "kind": "method", "line": 1656, "name": "spell_out", "signature": "def spell_out(s)"}, {"doc": "Truncate ``text`` for debug logs so we don't spam the terminal.", "kind": "method", "line": 1684, "name": "_summarise", "signature": "def _summarise(text, max_len)"}, {"doc": "Play the success / error beeps and a reference tone, then return.\n\nUsed by ``--play-test-beeps`` to isolate \"speech audible, beeps\nnot\" issues without going through mic + flow.  Plays in order:\n\n1. Success beep (ascending two-tone, ~0.41 s incl. pad).\n2. One second of silence.\n3. Error beep (descending two-tone, ~0.48 s incl. pad).\n4. One second of silence.\n5. A 500 ms 440 Hz reference tone at ~0.5 amplitude — twice as\n   loud as the beeps' 0.25 amplitude — so a \"reference audible\n   but beeps not\" outcome points at the beep waveform (raise\n   amplitude or extend the lead-silence pad) rather than at\n   the audio stack.\n\nRoutes through the same :class:`TextToSpeech` instance that the\nmain flow would use, so the diagnostic exercises the exact same\nstream-open / play / wait code path (and thus the same\nPortAudio / PipeWire / ALSA shim) that the real beeps go\nthrough.", "kind": "method", "line": 1704, "name": "_run_beep_diagnostic", Lines that open *after* TTS ends are accepted\nwith no added latency – the user can talk the moment the\nassistant stops, no grace window required.\n\nOnly takes effect when ``ignore_stt_during_tts`` is on; when\nit's off (true barge-in mode) we leave the set empty so every\nline completes through to :meth:`process_utterance`.", "kind": "method", "line": 712, "name": "on_line_started", "signature": "def on_line_started(self, event)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 746, "name": "on_line_completed", "signature": "def on_line_completed(self, event)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 772, "name": "on_error", "signature": "def on_error(self, event)"}, {"doc": "Route an utterance.\n\nReturns ``True`` if it was consumed by a flow or a global handler,\n``False`` otherwise. Returns ``True`` if there was one.", "kind": "method", "line": 1156, "name": "cancel_active", "signature": "def cancel_active(self)"}, {"doc": "Speak ``text`` through the configured TTS, outside any flow.\n\nPublic counterpart to flows yielding ``d.say(...)``: lets the\napplication deliver welcome messages, status announcements,\nerror notifications, and the like without first registering a\nsingle-shot flow.  Safe to call concurrently with an active\nflow – it just routes through the same ``_speak`` path the\nrunner uses for in-flow prompts, so:\n\n* ``mute_fn`` is invoked around playback (if configured) so\n  the mic is silenced while the assistant talks.\n* ``_speaking`` is set across playback and the\n  ``on_line_started`` hook tags any STT lines that open during\n  this window as self-capture, so they get dropped on\n  completion (when ``ignore_stt_during_tts`` is on).\n* ``log_io`` emits a clean ``assistant: ...`` line, matching\n  the format used for in-flow speech.\n\nBlocks until playback finishes – mirrors the behaviour of an\nin-flow ``Say``.  Empty / ``None`` ``text`` is a no-op. This routes through\nthe configured ``success_beep_fn`` / ``error_beep_fn`` (or\ntheir ``tts.play_*`` auto-wiring) and provides three levels\nof visibility for \"no beep heard\" debugging:\n\n* No-op when the callback is not configured, but the\n  first such miss for each kind is reported once on\n  stderr so the auto-wiring failing silently doesn't\n  look like a configured-but-broken beep.  Subsequent\n  misses are quiet to keep the log readable.\n* Callback exceptions are *always* reported on stderr\n  (regardless of ``debug``) — a broken beep callback is\n  rare, surprising, and worth surfacing on the first\n  occurrence; we don't want it swallowed.\n* Successful invocations emit a debug trace via\n  :meth:`_log` so you can confirm the runner reached the\n  beep and on which path (turn it on with ``debug=True``).", "kind": "method", "line": 1504, "name": "_play_beep", "signature": "def _play_beep(self, kind)"}, {"doc": "Play the \"recognized\" cue, if a beep callback is wired.\n\nFired before the TTS reply on every recognized utterance:\ntrigger matches, completed alphanumeric input, and matched\nconfirm / choose / free-form answers.", "kind": "method", "line": 1551, "name": "_play_success_beep", "signature": "def _play_success_beep(self)"}, {"doc": "Play the \"not recognized\" cue, if a beep callback is wired.\n\nFired when an utterance can't be routed: no trigger matched,\nan active flow couldn't interpret it (reprompt / abandon),\nor the runner is unmounted entirely.", "kind": "method", "line": 1560, "name": "_play_error_beep", "signature": "def _play_error_beep(self)"}, {"doc": "Speak ``\"deleting <spoken_form(character)>\"`` after an UNDO.\n\nInvoked from :meth:`_interpret_alphanumeric` when a \"delete\" /\n\"backspace\" / \"undo\" / \"scratch that\" command pops a character\noff the in-progress buffer (and ``spell_feedback=True``). (0.92)\n\nExample as TranscriptEventListener:\n    >>> recognizer = IntentRecognizer(\"path/to/embedding-model\")\n    >>> recognizer.register_intent(\"turn on the lights\", lambda c, u, s: print(f\"Lights on!\"))\n    >>> transcriber.add_listener(recognizer)  # Now intents are recognized automatically", "kind": "class", "line": 42, "name": "IntentRecognizer", "signature": "class IntentRecognizer(TranscriptEventListener)"}, {"doc": "Alias for ``canonical_phrase`` (backward compatibility).", "kind": "method", "line": 37, "name": "trigger_phrase", "signature": "def trigger_phrase(self)"}, {"doc": "Initialize an intent recognizer.\n\nArgs:\n    model_path: Path to the directory containing the embedding model files\n               (ONNX model and tokenizer.bin).\n    model_arch: The embedding model architecture to use.\n               Currently only GEMMA_300M is supported.\n    model_variant: Model variant to load: \"fp32\", \"fp16\", \"q8\", \"q4\",\n                  or \"q4f16\". routed through the say queue so it plays in\nthe same order as any in-flight :meth:`TextToSpeech.say` calls\nrather than racing ahead on the play queue.\n\n``kind`` selects which packaged WAV to play:\n\n* ``\"error\"`` – ``assets/error.wav``, played to signal a\n  misrecognition or a rejected utterance.\n* ``\"success\"`` – ``assets/success.wav``, played to signal a\n  recognized utterance, just before the TTS response.", "kind": "class", "line": 51, "name": "_BeepRequest", "signature": "class _BeepRequest"}, {"doc": "Return ``(samples_float32, sample_rate)`` for the named beep.\n\nLoaded lazily from the packaged ``assets/<kind>.wav`` file the first\ntime it's requested and cached for the lifetime of the process.\nRaises :class:`ValueError` for unknown kinds and lets file errors\nfrom :func:`load_wav_file` propagate (so a missing asset is loud,\nnot silent — the symptom otherwise would be the same \"no beep\"\nissue we just spent two iterations debugging).", "kind": "method", "line": 88, "name": "_load_beep_samples", "signature": "def _load_beep_samples(np, kind)"}, {"doc": "Import numpy and sounddevice for `TextToSpeech.say`; raise MoonshineError if missing.", "kind": "method", "line": 116, "name": "_import_say_audio_deps", "signature": "def _import_say_audio_deps()"}, {"doc": "Return PortAudio's current default output device index, if any.\n\nWraps ``sd.default.device`` because sounddevice exposes that as a\ncustom ``_InputOutputPair`` NamedTuple, *not* a plain ``tuple`` /\n``list``, so an ``isinstance(..., (tuple, list))`` check on it\nmisses and the diagnostic flag would silently never light up.\nFalls back through several access patterns so a minor sounddevice\nAPI change can't suppress the \"current default\" annotation.", "kind": "method", "line": 129, "name": "_resolve_default_output_index", "signature": "def _resolve_default_output_index(sd)"}, {"doc": "Return human-readable output device descriptions for diagnostics.\n\nEach entry is formatted ``\"[idx] name (hostapi: NAME)\"`` so a\ncaller can paste either the index or a substring of the name into\n:class:`TextToSpeech`'s ``output_device`` argument (or the\n``--output-device`` flag of the CLI demo).  The first line of the\nreturned list flags PortAudio's default output device — on\nRaspberry Pi this is often *not* the one with speakers attached\n(e.g. HDMI when the user has wired up the 3.5 mm jack), and a\nsilent assistant with no errors in the logs is exactly the\nsymptom of the wrong device being selected.\n\nUse :class:`TextToSpeech`'s ``output_device`` to pin to a\nspecific one when ``None`` (= host default) doesn't reach a\nspeaker.", "kind": "method", "line": 163, "name": "list_output_devices", "signature": "def list_output_devices()"}, {"doc": "PortAudio device indices with at least one output channel, and host API name.", "kind": "method", "line": 219, "name": "_say_enumerate_output_devices", "signature": "def _say_enumerate_output_devices(sd)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 241, "name": "_say_device_lines", "signature": "def _say_device_lines(outs)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 245, "name": "_say_device_spec_key", "signature": "def _say_device_spec_key(device)"}, {"doc": "Pick the best output sample rate the device will actually open.\n\nReturns ``(target_sr, last_error)``. ``target_sr`` is ``None`` if no\ncandidate rate works (in which case ``last_error`` is the PortAudio\nerror from the source-rate probe and useful for diagnostics).\nOtherwise ``target_sr`` is:\n\n1. ``source_sr`` if the device accepts it natively (no resampling),\n2. 48000 Hz when supported (cleanest fallback for 24 kHz input),\n3. otherwise the largest supported rate that is an integer multiple\n   or divisor of ``source_sr``,\n4. otherwise the supported rate closest to ``source_sr``.\n\nProbes that fail with ``paDeviceUnavailable`` (-9985) are retried\na few times with a short backoff: that error code is transient on\nexclusive-access ALSA devices (e.g. USB DACs) when a previous\n``sd.play()`` stream hasn't fully released the device yet, and a\nsingle failed probe shouldn't be enough to disqualify a rate the\ndevice actually supports.", "kind": "method", "line": 270, "name": "_select_output_sample_rate", "signature": "def _select_output_sample_rate(sd)"}, {"doc": "Numpy-only linear-interpolation resample of mono float32 audio.\n\nLinear interpolation is the highest-quality resampler we can build\nwithout scipy; for clean integer ratios (e.g. 24 kHz -> 48 kHz) the\nnew sample positions land exactly between source samples, so the\ninterpolation error stays small.", "kind": "method", "line": 339, "name": "_resample_linear", "signature": "def _resample_linear(np, samples, source_sr, target_sr)"}, {"doc": "Return ``(pcm, sample_rate)`` from a ``clone`` spec.\n\nAccepts either a path to a WAV file on disk (``str`` / ``Path``), which is\ndecoded with :func:`moonshine_voice.utils.load_wav_file` (16/24-bit PCM,\nstereo mixed down to mono), or a ``(pcm, sample_rate)`` pair where ``pcm``\nis mono float PCM in ``[-1, 1]`` (any sequence or numpy array) and\n``sample_rate`` is in Hz.", "kind": "method", "line": 360, "name": "_normalize_clone_argument", "signature": "def _normalize_clone_argument(clone)"}, {"doc": "Transcribe a clone reference clip so ZipVoice gets text aligned with the audio.", "kind": "method", "line": 389, "name": "_autotranscribe_clone_pcm", "signature": "def _autotranscribe_clone_pcm(pcm, sample_rate)"}, {"doc": "Return PortAudio output device index, or None for the host default stream device.", "kind": "method", "line": 423, "name": "_say_resolve_output_index", "signature": "def _say_resolve_output_index(spec_key, outs)"}, {"doc": "On-device TTS using Moonshine (Kokoro / Piper and language assets under ``g2p_root``).\n\nRequired assets are resolved with ``moonshine_get_tts_dependencies`` and, unless you pass\n``download=False`` and ``asset_root``, downloaded from ``https://download.moonshine.ai/tts/``.\n\nThe ``language`` tag is validated against the native TTS catalog before download\n(`MoonshineTtsLanguageError` lists supported tags).     If ``voice`` is set, it is checked against\nvoices reported as ``found`` for that language under the resolved asset root\n(`MoonshineTtsVoiceError` lists downloaded ids then catalog ids available for download).\nWith ``download=True``, a voice that is catalogued but not yet on disk is downloaded automatically.\nUse a ``kokoro_``, ``piper_``, or ``zipvoice_`` prefix on ``voice`` to pin the vocoder (e.g.\n``kokoro_af_heart``, ``zipvoice_american_female``). ZipVoice is a zero-shot voice cloner: besides\nthe built-in ``zipvoice_<id>`` reference voices you can clone your own by passing ``clone`` —\neither a path to a ``.wav`` file or a ``(pcm, sample_rate)`` pair of mono float PCM — along with\n(recommended) ``clone_transcript``, the text spoken in the reference clip (when omitted, the clip\nis auto-transcribed with Moonshine ASR before cloning). When ``clone`` is set\nthe ZipVoice engine is used automatically; passing ``voice`` together with ``clone``\nraises `MoonshineError`.\nUse `list_tts_languages` and\n`list_tts_voices` (``present`` / ``downloadable``) or `get_tts_voice_catalog` to discover options.", "kind": "class", "line": 453, "name": "TextToSpeech", "signature": "class TextToSpeech"}, {"doc": "Parse ``KEY=value`` pairs from repeated ``--options`` (values stay strings except booleans).", "kind": "method", "line": 1333, "name": "_parse_options_cli", "signature": "def _parse_options_cli(pairs)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1356, "name": "_write_wav_mono_pcm16", "signature": "def _write_wav_mono_pcm16(path, samples, sample_rate_hz)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 295, "name": "_try", "signature": "def _try(sr)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 477, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, language)"}, {"doc": "Shared playback/queue state used by both the from-files and ZipVoice-from-memory paths.", "kind": "method", "line": 604, "name": "_init_playback_state", "signature": "def _init_playback_state(self, output_device, volume, debug)"}, {"doc": "Create a ZipVoice synthesizer from an in-memory reference clip (mono float PCM).", "kind": "method", "line": 636, "name": "_init_zipvoice_from_clone", "signature": "def _init_zipvoice_from_clone(self, language)"}, {"doc": "Print a one-liner identifying the PortAudio device we opened.\n\nEmitted only when ``debug=True`` (silent during normal use). When enabled\nit helps diagnose a silent runtime with no errors in the trace, which is\nalmost always the *wrong* PortAudio device being selected (e.g. HDMI on a\nPi when speakers are on the 3.5 mm jack); the log shows *which* device the\nworker actually opened.\n\nIncludes the host-API name and the default sample rate the\ndevice claims to support; on top of that, when the resolved\ndevice is the host default we list the other available\noutputs so the user can pin a specific one via\n``TextToSpeech(output_device=...)`` (or the CLI's\n``--output-device`` flag).\n\nOnly emitted when ``debug=True``; it is silent during normal use.", "kind": "method", "line": 734, "name": "_announce_resolved_device", "signature": "def _announce_resolved_device(self, sd, resolved)"}, {"doc": "Emit a timestamped trace line to stderr when ``debug=True``.\n\nSame shape as ``DialogFlow._log`` so traces from the two\ncomponents can be read together: each line shows the wall\ntime since the previous log line and since the first log\nline of this instance.  Off by default — TTS traces are\nverbose and only useful for diagnosing playback problems\n(e.g. why a beep didn't seem to play).", "kind": "method", "line": 793, "name": "_log", "signature": "def _log(self, msg)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 819, "name": "_c_options_for_create", "signature": "def _c_options_for_create(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 828, "name": "language", "signature": "def language(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 832, "name": "asset_root", "signature": "def asset_root(self)"}, {"doc": "Synthesize ``text`` to PCM float samples ``(-1..1)`` and sample rate in Hz.", "kind": "method", "line": 835, "name": "synthesize", "signature": "def synthesize(self, text)"}, {"doc": "Synthesize speech directly from IPA ``phonemes``, skipping grapheme-to-phoneme conversion.\n\n``phonemes`` is an International Phonetic Alphabet string in the same format produced by\n:meth:`~moonshine_voice.g2p.GraphemeToPhonemizer.to_ipa`. Passing the raw\nphonemes for the same language yields audio equivalent to :meth:`synthesize` on the original\ntext, but lets you inspect or edit the phonemes in between (e.g. to fix a name's\npronunciation). Returns PCM float samples ``(-1..1)`` and the sample rate in Hz.", "kind": "method", "line": 856, "name": "synthesize_from_phonemes", "signature": "def synthesize_from_phonemes(self, phonemes)"}, {"doc": "Queue ``text`` for synthesis and playback, returning immediately.\n\n``text`` may be a single string or a list of strings. A list is equivalent to calling\n``say`` once per element in order.\n\nUtterances are played in order. Synthesis of the next utterance is pipelined with playback\nof the current one so there is minimal gap between consecutive utterances. Call `stop` to\ncancel all pending utterances and halt the currently-playing audio.\n\nUses `synthesize` for audio generation; ``options`` is passed through unchanged.\n\n``device`` may be ``None`` (host default output), a PortAudio device index, a decimal string\nindex, or a substring of the device name (case-insensitive). If there are no output devices,\nthe index is invalid, or no name matches, the error is raised on the calling thread before\nthe utterance is enqueued.", "kind": "method", "line": 883, "name": "say", "signature": "def say(self, text)"}, {"doc": "Play the bundled \"error\" beep and return immediately.\n\nPlays ``assets/error.wav`` queued through the same pipeline as\n:meth:`say` — so if a previous ``say`` hasn't finished speaking\nyet the beep plays right after it, rather than racing ahead.\nUse :meth:`wait` / :meth:`is_talking` to track playback.\n\nPairs with :meth:`play_success`: callers that want audible\nfeedback for whether speech recognition succeeded can call\n:meth:`play_success` on a recognized utterance and\n:meth:`play_error` on an unrecognized one.\n\n``device`` accepts the same values as :meth:`say` (``None`` =\nconstructor's ``output_device`` if set, otherwise host\ndefault; a PortAudio index, a decimal string index, or a\ncase-insensitive device-name substring).  Honouring the\nconstructor's ``output_device`` here matches :meth:`say`'s\nbehaviour — without that, callers who pin a specific output\ndevice for speech would get their cue beeps routed to the\nhost default and end up with audible speech but inaudible\nbeeps.", "kind": "method", "line": 928, "name": "play_error", "signature": "def play_error(self)"}, {"doc": "Play the bundled \"success\" beep and return immediately.\n\nCounterpart to :meth:`play_error` for positive feedback: plays\n``assets/success.wav`` confirming that the most recent\nutterance was recognized / accepted.  Same queueing rules as\n:meth:`play_error` — decoded once, cached, and ordered\nthrough the say queue so it never races ahead of an in-flight\n:meth:`say`.\n\n``device`` accepts the same values as :meth:`say` and falls\nback to the constructor's ``output_device`` when ``None``,\nfor the same reason as :meth:`play_error`.", "kind": "method", "line": 962, "name": "play_success", "signature": "def play_success(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 987, "name": "_ensure_say_workers", "signature": "def _ensure_say_workers(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1005, "name": "_synth_worker", "signature": "def _synth_worker(self)"}, {"doc": "Synthesize a single utterance into a _PlayItem (runs on synthesis thread).", "kind": "method", "line": 1060, "name": "_synthesize_one", "signature": "def _synthesize_one(self, req, np)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1069, "name": "_play_worker", "signature": "def _play_worker(self)"}, {"doc": "Resolve the device and play a single synthesized utterance (runs on playback thread).", "kind": "method", "line": 1097, "name": "_play_one", "signature": "def _play_one(self, item, sd, np)"}, {"doc": "Return ``True`` if utterances are queued, being synthesized, or currently playing.", "kind": "method", "line": 1242, "name": "is_talking", "signature": "def is_talking(self)"}, {"doc": "Block until all queued utterances have been synthesized and played.", "kind": "method", "line": 1255, "name": "wait", "signature": "def wait(self)"}, {"doc": "Clear the utterance queue and stop any audio currently playing.\n\nReturns once all pending utterances are discarded and the active playback (if any) has\nbeen halted. It is safe to call `say` again afterwards.", "kind": "method", "line": 1260, "name": "stop", "signature": "def stop(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1288, "name": "close", "signature": "def close(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1320, "name": "__enter__", "signature": "def __enter__(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1323, "name": "__exit__", "signature": "def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1326, "name": "__del__", "signature": "def __del__(self)"}]}, {"id": "python/src/moonshine_voice/utils.py", "kind": "module", "label": "utils.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "32b527b32392b85e", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"doc": "Get the path to the assets directory included in the package.\n\nReturns:\n    Path object pointing to the assets directory\n\nExample:\n    >>> from moonshine_voice.utils import get_assets_path\n    >>> assets_path = get_assets_path()\n    >>> model_path = assets_path / \"tiny-en\"", "kind": "function", "line": 9, "name": "get_assets_path", "signature": "def get_assets_path()"}, {"doc": "Get the path to a specific model directory in the assets folder.\n\nArgs:\n    model_name: Name of the model directory (default: \"tiny-en\")\n\nReturns:\n    Path object pointing to the model directory\n\nExample:\n    >>> from moonshine_voice.utils import get_model_path\n    >>> model_path = get_model_path(\"tiny-en\")\n    >>> transcriber = Transcriber(str(model_path))", "kind": "function", "line": 27, "name": "get_model_path", "signature": "def get_model_path(model_name)"}, {"doc": "Load a WAV file and return audio data as float array and sample rate.\n\nSupports 16-bit and 24-bit PCM WAV files. Audio samples are normalized\nto the range [-1.0, 1.0].\n\nArgs:\n    file_path: Path to the WAV file\n\nReturns:\n    Tuple of (audio_data, sample_rate) where:\n    - audio_data: List of float samples in range [-1.0, 1.0]\n    - sample_rate: Sample rate in Hz\n\nRaises:\n    ValueError: If the file is not a valid WAV file\n    IOError: If the file cannot be read\n\nExample:\n    >>> from moonshine_voice.utils import load_wav_file\n    >>> audio_data, sample_rate = load_wav_file(\"audio.wav\")\n    >>> print(f\"Loaded {len(audio_data)} samples at {sample_rate} Hz\")", "kind": "function", "line": 47, "name": "load_wav_file", "signature": "def load_wav_file(file_path)"}]}, {"id": "python/tests/test_cli.py", "kind": "module", "label": "test_cli.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "3d58cbfe2b256855", "symbol_count": 8, "symbols": [{"doc": "Locate the installed console script, falling back to ``python -m``.\n\nConsole scripts are installed next to the interpreter running the tests, so\nwe look there first (this is the wheel-under-test in CI). into first-party core code. See core/STYLE_GUIDE.md for the rationale. Runs anywhere (macOS/Linux), needs only bash + grep + find, and is registered as the `check-banned-constructs` ctest.  Two tiers of enforcement:  1. Hard ban (zero tolerance, everywhere in first-party code): unsafe C string functions that have safe, bounded replacements.  2. Baseline gate (regression only): owning new/delete, C allocation calls, reinterpret_cast, and non-standard compiler builtins (__builtin_*, a GCC/Clang extension MSVC rejects) are tolerated where they already exist (recorded in core/.banned-constructs-allowlist) but blocked in any file not on that list. As modules are cleaned up, regenerate the baseline with `scripts/check-banned-constructs.sh --update-baseline` to lock in the improvement.  Usage: scripts/check-banned-constructs.sh                 # check (default) scripts/check-banned-constructs.sh --update-baseline", "id": "scripts/check-banned-constructs.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "check-banned-constructs.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "e784602c5c5c93cc", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"doc": "Print repo-relative paths of first-party files matching a regex, sorted.", "kind": "function", "line": 76, "name": "scan"}]}, {"doc": "Gate clang-tidy findings against a committed baseline so that only *newly introduced* problems fail the reliability run. This mirrors the approach in check-banned-constructs.sh: the current first-party code has a known, curated set of findings (see core/.clang-tidy-baseline) that are either benign for our \"C++ as a better C\" style or deliberately deferred; we accept those but refuse to let new ones creep in.  The baseline key is \"<check-name>\\t<repo-relative-path>\" (not line numbers, so it is stable across edits and reformatting). A finding is \"new\" if that pair is absent from the baseline. Adding a genuinely new class of bug -- e.g. the first clang-analyzer null-dereference in a file that never had one -- therefore fails the run, while shuffling lines around in an already-flagged file does not.  Usage: check-clang-tidy.sh --log FILE --baseline FILE --repo-root DIR [--update]  --update   Regenerate the baseline from FILE instead of comparing. Use this after intentionally changing the code/config, then commit the updated baseline.  Exit status: 0 = no new findings (or --update succeeded); 1 = new findings; 2 = usage / environment error.", "id": "scripts/check-clang-tidy.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "check-clang-tidy.sh", "signature": "def render_header(data, source_name, optimization)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 159, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}]}, {"doc": "Fold one or more fixes into the current in-progress release by cherry-picking them onto its release-v<version> branch. No version bump and no tag: the release branch is the mutable source of truth, and build-all-platforms.sh refreshes the v<version> tag from the branch HEAD on its next run.  Usage: scripts/patch-release.sh <commit-ish> [<commit-ish> ...]  Example (fix already committed on main as abc1234): scripts/patch-release.sh abc1234  What it does: 1. Finds the newest release-v* branch (the release you're building). 2. Checks it out at origin's HEAD. 3. Cherry-picks the commits you name onto it. 4. Pushes the branch and returns you to main.  Afterwards re-run: scripts/build-all-platforms.sh It resumes (skipping completed stages) and the remaining stages pick up the new branch HEAD.  IMPORTANT: this is for a release that is still in progress. To ship a fix for a version that is ALREADY fully published, cut a NEW version with scripts/prepare-release.sh instead -- package registries reject re-uploading an existing version.", "id": "scripts/patch-release.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "patch-release.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "c211899532edcb62", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 32, "name": "main"}]}, {"doc": "============================================================================= Making a Release =============================================================================  A release lives on a per-release branch, release-v<version>, and every build/checkout step tracks that branch's HEAD. You never move tags or force-push by hand: build-all-platforms.sh derives and refreshes the v<version> tag from the branch automatically (the tag exists only because GitHub Releases and SwiftPM need one). So folding a fix into an in-progress release is just \"add a commit to the branch and re-run the build\".  1. Cut the release: scripts/prepare-release.sh 0.0.69 Creates branch release-v0.0.69 off origin/main, rewrites every version string via update-version.sh, commits, and pushes the branch. No tag is created here; you are dropped back on main so you can keep working.  2. Build and publish: scripts/build-all-platforms.sh Builds the newest release-v* branch (override with RELEASE_REF). The local platforms build in an isolated worktree at the branch HEAD; each remote host resets to the same branch HEAD. It is resumable: completed stages are skipped on re-run. build-all refreshes the v<version> tag to the branch HEAD so the publish steps / GitHub Releases have a tag.  3. Fold in a fix (same version, build incrementally): # commit the fix somewhere (e.g. on main), then: scripts/patch-release.sh <commit-ish>...", "id": "scripts/prepare-release.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "prepare-release.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "8a582e1ecbf4e59d", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"doc": "All imperative work lives inside main() so bash parses the whole script before executing anything (mirrors build-all-platforms.sh).", "kind": "function", "line": 67, "name": "main"}]}, {"id": "scripts/publish-binary.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "publish-binary.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "8539c414269238e8", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"id": "scripts/publish-examples.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "publish-examples.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "1847a9c406fa480c", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"id": "scripts/publish-swift.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "publish-swift.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "b8ab6085eb35beca", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"id": "scripts/quantize-streaming-model.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "quantize-streaming-model.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "4cb3b55e132b8d37", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"doc": "Runs the heavy reliability checks on a Linux x86 host with clang + libFuzzer. Normally invoked by scripts/reliability.sh over SSH, but can be run directly on the box from the repo root.  Steps (each contributes to the final pass/fail): 1. Configure + build core with -DMOONSHINE_RELIABILITY=ON (ASan/UBSan) using clang, exporting compile_commands.json. 2. Run the core test suite under the sanitizers. 3. ThreadSanitizer: build the threaded tests into a separate build dir with -DMOONSHINE_SANITIZER=thread and run them (advisory unless TSAN_STRICT=1). 4. Run clang-tidy on first-party sources and fail on any finding that is NOT already recorded in core/.clang-tidy-baseline (i.e. newly introduced). 5. Fuzz each per-module target for FUZZ_SECONDS, saving any crash reproducers.  Environment: FUZZ_SECONDS   seconds per fuzz target (default 900) TIDY_UPDATE_BASELINE  1 => regenerate core/.clang-tidy-baseline from this run instead of gating against it (commit the result). Never fails the run. Default 0. TSAN           1 => run the ThreadSanitizer stage (default 1); 0 to skip TSAN_STRICT    1 => TSan findings fail the run (default 0, advisory) TSAN_TEST_TIMEOUT  per-TSan-test wall-clock limit in seconds (default 600); a timeout is always a hard failure so a hang can't stall the pipeline for hours STREAM_MEMORY_TEST_TIMEOUT  wall-clock limit for transcriber-streaming- memory-test (default 900) MOONSHINE_STREAM_MEMORY_AUDIO_SECONDS  audio seconds fed by that test (default 120); forwarded to the test binary", "id": "scripts/reliability-remote.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "reliability-remote.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "379c57b144452afd", "symbol_count": 4, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 69, "name": "record_failure"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 89, "name": "require_tool"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 183, "name": "run_test"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 439, "name": "run_fuzzer"}]}, {"doc": "Periodic reliability driver. Run this from the Mac (or any dev machine). It:  1. Runs the fast, local static checks (formatting + banned constructs). 2. Syncs the working tree to a native Linux x86 box over SSH (so even uncommitted changes are exercised), preserving the box's large model / test assets. 3. Runs scripts/reliability-remote.sh there (ASan/UBSan build + test suite, clang-tidy, a ThreadSanitizer rebuild + threaded tests, a long-stream memory regression test, and time-boxed per-module fuzzing). 4. Copies logs and any crash reproducers back to core/reliability/artifacts.  The whole run is designed to finish within a few hours (tune FUZZ_SECONDS).  Usage: scripts/reliability.sh  Environment: RELIABILITY_HOST   SSH host of the Linux x86 box (default: petes-alienware-pc) REMOTE_DIR         repo path on that box, relative to $HOME (default: moonshine) FUZZ_SECONDS       seconds per fuzz target (default 900 => ~1h of fuzzing) TIDY_UPDATE_BASELINE 1 => regenerate core/.clang-tidy-baseline from this run (copied back locally to commit) instead of gating on it TSAN               1 => run the ThreadSanitizer stage (default 1); 0 to skip TSAN_STRICT        1 => TSan findings fail the run (default 0, advisory)  The local static checks (banned constructs + formatting) are hard gates: any failure aborts the run before syncing, so drift is never silently skipped. Run scripts/format-core.sh to fix formatting drift wholesale.", "id": "scripts/reliability.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "reliability.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "135956af9f059155", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"doc": "Benchmark to compare Moonshine and Whisper model latency in live speech scenarios.  This is an opinionated benchmark that looks at the latency and total compute cost of the two families of models in a situation that is representative of many common real-time voice applications' requirements:  - Speech needs to be responded to as quickly as possible once a user completes a phrase. - The phrases are of durations between a range of one to ten seconds.  These are very different requirements from bulk offline processing scenarios, where the overall throughput of the system is more important, and so the latency on a single segment of speech is less important than the overall throughput of the system. This allows optimizations like batch processing.  We are not claiming that Whisper is not a great model for offline processing, but we do want to highlight the advantages we that Moonshine offers for live speech applications with real-time latency requirements.  The experimental setup is as follows:  - We use the two_cities.wav audio file as a test case, since it has a mix of short and long phrases. You can vary this by passing in your own audio file with the --wav_path argument. - We use the Moonshine Tiny, Base, Tiny Streaming, Small Streaming, and Medium Streaming models. - We compare these to the Whisper Tiny, Base, Small, and Large v3 models. Since the Moonshine Medium Streaming model achieves lower WER than Whisper Large v3 we compare those two, otherwise we compare each with their namesake. - We use the Moonshine VAD segmenter to split the audio into phrases, and feed each phrase to Whisper for transcription.", "id": "scripts/run-benchmarks.py", "kind": "module", "label": "run-benchmarks.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "2d4afeeeb65c12fa", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"kind": "class", "line": 132, "name": "WhisperListener", "signature": "class WhisperListener(TranscriptEventListener)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 133, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 137, "name": "on_line_completed", "signature": "def on_line_completed(self, event)"}]}, {"doc": "One-time setup of the Android toolchain needed to run the moonshine-voice instrumentation tests (scripts/test-android.sh) on an x86_64 Linux host with KVM. Everything installs under $HOME (no sudo), EXCEPT KVM group membership, which must be granted separately once:  sudo usermod -aG kvm \"$USER\"   # then log out/in (or reboot)  Installs: Temurin JDK 17, Android command-line tools, platform-tools, emulator, the compileSdk platform + build-tools, the NDK + CMake pinned by build.gradle.kts, an x86_64 system image, and an AVD for it.", "id": "scripts/setup-android-ci.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "setup-android-ci.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "af64be2490cf0782", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 27, "name": "log"}]}, {"doc": "Run the moonshine-voice Android library's instrumentation tests on a real device or emulator (./gradlew connectedAndroidTest). Unlike scripts/build- android.sh (which only builds the AAR) and scripts/test-examples.sh (which only compiles the example apps), this actually installs and runs the library on an Android runtime, so it is the real validation of the library on a device: a successful link does not prove the bundled ONNX Runtime's symbols resolve on an older OS, but running the tests on a matching-API emulator does. The library's minSdk comes from build.gradle.kts; boot an emulator at (or above) that API to exercise the supported floor.  Usage: ./scripts/test-android.sh [--avd NAME] [--serial SERIAL]  Options: --avd NAME      Boot this AVD headless, wait for it, run the tests, then shut it down on exit. Without --avd, a device/emulator must already be connected (see --serial). --serial SERIAL Target a specific adb device/emulator serial.  Environment: ANDROID_HOME or ANDROID_SDK_ROOT — required.  ABI note: the library ships native libs for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 (see build.gradle.kts abiFilters), so the device/emulator's ABI must be one of those. On Apple Silicon use an \"arm64-v8a\" system image; x86_64 emulators only run on an x86_64 host. Apple Silicon cannot run armeabi-v7a (32-bit ARM) emulators; test that ABI on a real 32-bit-capable device via --serial.", "id": "scripts/test-android.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "test-android.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "900b86ce6463ac57", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 37, "name": "log"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 38, "name": "die"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 82, "name": "cleanup"}]}, {"id": "scripts/test-core.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "test-core.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "5dd8c7744c618a4e", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"doc": "Tests that the code in the documentation still works, by executing the fenced code blocks in README.md and python/README.md (see python/tests/test_docs.py) and running the getting-started notebook end to end, all against a freshly built wheel.  The Python module tests (python/tests/test_modules.py) are run separately by scripts/test-python.sh.  Usage: ./scripts/test-docs.sh                Build the wheel first, then test. ./scripts/test-docs.sh --skip-build   Reuse the wheel already in python/dist/ (faster iteration).", "id": "scripts/test-docs.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "test-docs.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "fa2485d088762a0b", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 31, "name": "cleanup"}]}, {"doc": "Verify iOS and Android examples build standalone: either from GitHub Release archives (default) or from a temporary copy of examples/android and examples/ios (--local-examples).  Usage: ./scripts/test-examples.sh [--repo OWNER/REPO] [--tag vX.Y.Z] [--workdir DIR] [--keep-workdir] ./scripts/test-examples.sh --local-examples [--workdir DIR] [--keep-workdir] ./scripts/test-examples.sh --local-library [--workdir DIR]  With --local-examples, skips GitHub downloads and copies this repository's examples/android and examples/ios into a temp tree (same layout as extracted release archives), then runs the same Gradle / xcodebuild checks.  With --local-library (implies --local-examples), the examples are built against THIS checkout's library instead of the published artifacts, so you can verify a library change (e.g. a new API or a lowered minSdk) before publishing: - Android: builds + installs the AAR into the local Maven cache (via scripts/build-android.sh local), injects mavenLocal() as the first repository (via a Gradle init script) so it takes precedence, and syncs each example's requested moonshine-voice version to this checkout's coordinates(). The example apps' minSdk (like the library's) comes from their Gradle files. - iOS/macOS: copies this checkout's swift/ package into the temp iOS tree and rewrites each example's project.pbxproj to reference that local package (XCLocalSwiftPackageReference) instead of the remote moonshine-swift Git package. Requires swift/Moonshine.xcframework to exist; when it is missing, scripts/build-swift.sh is run to build it first.  Environment: ANDROID_HOME or ANDROID_SDK_ROOT — required for Android (unless SKIP_ANDROID=1)", "id": "scripts/test-examples.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "test-examples.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "1e8f42ba85ccf8ac", "symbol_count": 23, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 56, "name": "usage"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 94, "name": "log"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 98, "name": "die"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 157, "name": "cleanup"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 169, "name": "download_url_for"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 178, "name": "download_one"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 194, "name": "extract_tgz"}, {"doc": "List immediate child directories of examples/<platform>/ (used to know which release assets to download: <platform>-<dirname>.tar.gz).", "kind": "function", "line": 204, "name": "list_example_project_names"}, {"doc": "Download every <platform>-<project>.tar.gz for that platform and extract into dest_root (same layout as the old monolithic *-examples.tar.gz).", "kind": "function", "line": 213, "name": "download_platform_example_archives"}, {"doc": "Copy examples/android and examples/ios from the repository (parent of scripts/) into the same layout used after extracting the release tarballs.", "kind": "function", "line": 230, "name": "copy_local_example_trees"}, {"doc": "Portable in-place edit (BSD/macOS sed and GNU sed differ on -i), applied to each given file with the supplied sed expression.", "kind": "function", "line": 247, "name": "portable_sed_inplace"}, {"doc": "Read the moonshine-voice version this checkout would publish, parsed from the root build.gradle.kts coordinates(\"ai.moonshine\", \"moonshine-voice\", \"X.Y.Z\").", "kind": "function", "line": 260, "name": "read_library_version"}, {"doc": "Build the AAR from this checkout and install it into the local Maven cache so the example builds can resolve it. For a strategically sampled set of configurations (one per code path, biased toward the smallest model that exercises it), this script: 1. asks the C API (via moonshine-download-smoke) for the download manifest, 2. downloads every listed file into a fresh temp directory with curl, 3. loads the corresponding engine from that directory and runs one trivial inference.  If a required file is missing from a manifest, step 3 fails - which is the whole point: this verifies the catalog lists everything each model needs.  After the native samples, it also drives the framework-level download tests that exercise the real AssetDownloader on each platform (they are opt-in and skip on a plain `swift test` / `connectedAndroidTest`): - Swift: MOONSHINE_DOWNLOAD_TESTS=1 swift test --filter AssetDownloaderNetworkTests (macOS, when `swift` and swift/Moonshine.xcframework are present). - Android: connectedAndroidTest for AssetDownloaderTest with moonshineDownloadTests=1 (only when a device/emulator is already connected; this script never boots one - use scripts/test-android.sh for emulator lifecycle).  This test hits the network, so it is intentionally NOT part of the hermetic scripts/test-core.sh. Run it directly (it assumes a fast connection) or from scripts/build-all-platforms.sh / CI. Pass --all to cover more configurations (extra languages and embedding variants) for nightly runs. No gain here -- the VAD front-end is robust to level, and the STT clip is level-normalized in one shot before its log-mel (see the note just before g_stt_log_mel->Compute below). We keep the raw level for the VAD.  The slide is ESSENTIAL: without it every hop overwrites the same tail region and window[0 .. WS-HOP) stays at its initial zeros, so the STT only ever sees the single newest 32 ms hop (silence at kSpeechEnd) -- i.e. "silence + a tiny burst at the end", rms ~0. The VAD is unaffected because it reads the freshly written window[WS-HOP] directly.*

#### `main_i2s_audio_test.cc`
**Path:** `micro/examples/rp2350/src/main_i2s_audio_test.cc`
**File Doc:** *Standalone speaker / audio-output bring-up test (the `moonshine_micro_i2s_audio_test` target). It proves the I2S amp + speaker are wired up and making sound, driven by the same I2sAudioOutput backend the live apps use. Besides tones and recorded clips it also runs the neural TTS engine (the same one the live apps speak with) so the whole render path is exercised -- it does NOT touch the VAD/STT capture pipeline.  Designed for the Adafruit MAX98357A I2S class-D amp (#3006, https://www.adafruit.com/product/3006), which has its own I2S DAC -- so unlike the old PWM speaker there is no carrier and no RC reconstruction filter. Connect your own 4-8 ohm speaker to the amp's screw terminals.  Wiring (see src/i2s_out.pio; LRC = BCLK + 1 for the sideset pair):  Vin  -> Pico VSYS   (physical pin 39)   ; 2.5-5.5 V; use VSYS not VBUS GND  -> Pico GND    (physical pin 38) DIN  -> GP10        (physical pin 14)   ; I2S data BCLK -> GP11        (physical pin 15)   ; bit clock LRC  -> GP12        (physical pin 16)   ; word select (LRCLK) GAIN -> (leave open -> 9 dB)   SD -> (leave open -> enabled, (L+R)/2 mono)  GP10/11/12 are chosen so they don't collide with the I2S mic test (GP0/1/2). What you should hear: a rising A-major arpeggio, then a tone sweep, then 1 s recordings of "a", "b", "c", then the neural TTS voice saying the letters "a"/"b"/"c" and the words "hello"/"wifi", looping.  include <cmath> include <cstddef> include <cstdint> include <cstdio>*

#### `main_i2s_mic_test.cc`
**Path:** `micro/examples/rp2350/src/main_i2s_mic_test.cc`
**File Doc:** *Standalone I2S microphone bring-up test (the `moonshine_micro_i2s_mic_test` target). It does NOT touch the VAD/STT/TTS pipeline -- it only proves that an Adafruit SPH0645 I2S MEMS mic (https://www.adafruit.com/product/3421) is wired up and producing audio.  Wiring (matches the arduino-pico I2SInput.ino example the user followed):  mic DOUT -> GPIO0   (data into the RP2350) mic BCLK <- GPIO1   (bit clock, driven by the RP2350) mic LRCL <- GPIO2   (word select; must be BCLK + 1 for the PIO sideset) mic SEL  -> GND     (puts the mono element on the LEFT channel) mic GND  <-> GND mic 3V   <-> 3V3 (OUT)  Each cycle: record 5 s at 16 kHz, print per-channel stats, then (if USB is connected) stream the clip to the host for 5 s of playback. The device waits for CLIP_ACK from usb_audio_bridge.py before recording again so the host does not fall behind. Plain monitor.sh still works for the text stats only.  include <algorithm> include <cmath> include <cstdint> include <cstdio> include <cstring>  include "hardware/clocks.h" include "hardware/pio.h" include "hardware/vreg.h" include "i2s_mic.pio.h" include "i2s_mic_process.h"*

#### `main_i2s_relay.cc`
**Path:** `micro/examples/rp2350/src/main_i2s_relay.cc`
**File Doc:** *Dumb PCM -> I2S relay (the `moonshine_micro_i2s_relay` target).  This firmware does NO synthesis, VAD or STT. It is the device half of the hardware-in-the-loop TTS eval harness (scripts/hw_tts_eval/): the laptop synthesizes speech, streams the raw PCM here over USB CDC, and this app plays it out the MAX98357A I2S amp so an external mic can record the real acoustic path. Keeping the device dumb means the loop measures the exact same I2sAudioOutput path the live apps use, with nothing else in the way.  Wiring (identical to moonshine_micro_i2s_audio_test; see src/i2s_out.pio): Vin  -> Pico VSYS (pin 39)   GND -> GND DIN  -> GP10   BCLK -> GP11   LRC -> GP12   (MAX98357A / Adafruit 3006) GAIN -> open (9 dB)   SD -> open (enabled, (L+R)/2 mono)  Protocol (line commands over CDC; binary PCM is framed, not line-based): PING              -> replies "PONG" PLAY <rate> <n>   -> then read `n` int16 LE samples, streamed in hops of up to kHop samples, each hop prefixed by the 0xA5 0x5A sync (mirrors usb_audio_io.cc). Samples are written to I2sAudioOutput at <rate> Hz. When done, replies "PLAYED <m>" with the number of samples actually played (m == n on a clean stream).  PICO_STDIO_DEFAULT_CRLF=0 (see CMakeLists.txt) keeps 0x0A/0x0D PCM bytes from being mangled on the way in, and keeps our text replies from getting CR injected on the way out.  include <cstdint> include <cstdio> include <cstdlib>*

**Functions:**
- `ReadLine` (line 71) `int ReadLine(char* buf, int maxlen)` - *Read one newline-terminated line into `buf` (NUL-terminated), blocking until a non-empty line arrives. Feeds the watchdog each idle slice. CR and LF both terminate; blank lines are skipped.*
- `ReadByteTimed` (line 88) `int ReadByteTimed(int timeout_ms)` - *Read one byte, waiting up to ~timeout_ms. Returns -1 on timeout.*
- `ReadHop` (line 98) `int ReadHop(int16_t* out, int n)` - *Scan for the 0xA5 0x5A sync, then read up to `n` int16 LE samples into `out`. Returns the number of samples read; a short return means the host stalled mid-hop (each sample byte read times out so a dropped frame can't wedge the device -- see the deadlock note in usb_audio_io.cc). Returns -1 if no sync arrives within ~2 s (host aborted the stream).*
- `PlayStream` (line 140) `int PlayStream(spelling::I2sAudioOutput& out, int rate, int total)` - *Receive `total` samples from the host into RAM, then play them to the I2S amp at `rate` Hz. Returns the number of samples played.  Why buffer the whole clip instead of streaming hop->FIFO directly: the PIO I2S TX FIFO is only a few frames deep, and reading a 512-sample hop over USB CDC (one getchar per byte) takes far longer than those few frames play out. A read-then-write loop therefore underruns the FIFO on every hop boundary -- the SM stalls mid-stream and the amp clicks, which sounds like continuous broadband static. Receiving the whole clip first (no real-time constraint; USB flow-control backpressures the host) then streaming RAM->FIFO keeps the FIFO fed faster than real time, so playback is glitch-free.*

#### `main_step7c_synthonly.cc`
**Path:** `micro/examples/rp2350/src/main_step7c_synthonly.cc`
**File Doc:** *Step 7c of the minimal bring-up ladder: the mirror image of step 7b. #### `log_mel.cc`
**Path:** `micro/feature-generation/src/log_mel.cc`
**File Doc:** *Heap-free log-mel spectrogram for the on-device build.  Reflect-pad (center=True), windowed STFT, squared-magnitude, Slaney mel filterbank, crop to target_frames, log(value + eps), per-clip mean/std normalisation with std clamped >= 1e-3.  The DIFFERENCES from the desktop port are all about memory:  1. Compute() takes a caller-supplied output buffer instead of returning std::vector. Saves 64 KB of heap traffic per call.  2. Reflect padding is done on-the-fly per sample inside the framing loop. The desktop port materialised a 16512-sample `padded` vector (~66 KB).  3. STFT + power-spectrum + filterbank multiply are FUSED into a single pass: for each output frame we compute one 257-bin power row on the stack, then immediately scatter it through the mel filterbank into one column of the output buffer. The desktop port allocated a full (n_freq, n_frames) power matrix (~200 KB) and a (n_mels, n_frames) mel matrix (~64 KB).  4. log() and normalisation run in-place on the output buffer. Saves another 64 KB.  With our defaults this drops peak per-call heap usage from ~450 KB to 0 (just ~5 KB on the stack for frame_buf, spectrum, and one power row). The window + filterbank still live as heap std::vector members of LogMelSpectrogram itself (84 KB total), allocated ONCE in the constructor.*

**Functions:**
- `ReflectIndex` (line 69) `inline int ReflectIndex(int i, int n)` - *Reflect index without duplicating the boundary. Matches torch.nn.functional.pad(x, (pad, pad), mode="reflect"): index -1 -> 1, -2 -> 2, ..., and on the right side, n -> n-2, n+1 -> n-3, ...  `n` is the original waveform length, `i` is the padded-coords index in [-pad, n + pad). The implementation handles only the edge regions: callers in the hot loop pass already-validated indices in [0, n) directly past this helper. We use it from the framing loop where we sometimes step a sample or two past either edge due to center padding.*
- `ToFloatSample` (line 87) `inline float ToFloatSample(float s)` - *Per-sample input conversion for ComputeImpl. Lets the STT clip be stored as raw int16 mic samples (half the SRAM of fp32) and converted to the [-1, 1] float the STFT expects at the single read site, with no precision loss (the samples originate as int16 anyway). The fp32 overload is the identity.*
- `ToFloatSample` (line 88) `inline float ToFloatSample(int16_t s)`
- `HzToMelSlaney` (line 92) `float HzToMelSlaney(float hz)`
- `MelToHzSlaney` (line 99) `float MelToHzSlaney(float mel)`
- `HannWindowPeriodic` (line 106) `std::vector<float> HannWindowPeriodic(int length)`

#### `feature_generation_test.cc`
**Path:** `micro/feature-generation/tests/feature_generation_test.cc`
**File Doc:** *Unit tests for the feature-generation module, using TFLM's micro_test.h.  Covers the shared building blocks (periodic Hann, Slaney mel scale) and the load-bearing invariant that MelStreamer (one FFT per non-overlapping block, ring buffer) produces the SAME normalised feature plane as the batch LogMelSpectrogram::Compute(center=false) over the same samples. That parity is what lets the streaming VAD front-end match the batch path the models expect.  Runs on the host (logic only -- no interpreter): link against the module, kissfft, and the host TFLM stub.  include "feature_generation/feature_generation.h"  include <cmath> include <vector>  include "kiss_fftr.h" include "tensorflow/lite/micro/testing/micro_test.h"*

Its sample-to-sample difference (taken by the caller) is the glottal flow derivative that actually excites the cascade.*

#### `tts_cli.cc`
**Path:** `micro/neural-tts/host/tts_cli.cc`
**File Doc:** *Native (desktop) driver for the on-device neural TTS engine.  Runs the EXACT C++ pipeline the RP2350 firmware runs -- shared g2p front end -> Klatt rule durations -> diphone/word unit selection -> int8 RVQ decode through the s16x8 TFLM graph -> WORLD-lite vocoder -- but on the host, using the portable TFLM reference kernels (see host/tflm_ref/) instead of CMSIS-NN. The flash pack is loaded from a .bin file rather than linked from flash.  This is the fast, flash-free equivalent of the `moonshine_micro_tts` firmware + tts_speak.py: same bytes in, same PCM out, no board required.  Usage: tts_cli "hello there" -o out.wav tts_cli --ipa "h@loU" -o hi.wav tts_cli --pack path/to/neural_tts_pack.bin "text" -o out.wav tts_cli "text" -o -            # raw int16 LE PCM to stdout  include <cstdint> include <cstdio> include <cstring> include <string> include <vector>  include "neural_tts/neural_tts.h"*

#### `neural_tts.cc`
**Path:** `micro/neural-tts/src/neural_tts.cc`
**File Doc:** *Black-box neural TTS pipeline (see neural_tts.h). Port of the host reference scripts/synth_diphone_world.py synthesize() with the shipping flag set; every stage is annotated with its Python counterpart.  Arena life cycle per chunk (all caller arena; the G2P front end's small std::string/vector transients are the only malloc heap use):  [plan: runs, D, parts, candidate sets, track, f0]   -- whole chunk [decode: PbDecoder (+TFLM arena), one-unit cache]   -- rolled back [render: WorldLiteSynth + kissfft plans in arena]    -- reuses decode's  The control track is materialized in the decoder's *quantized log domain* (int16, output_scale, benv as log10-amplitude): all assembly math (crossfades, gain EQ, timbre/energy offsets, declination) is additive there, and frames convert to linear WorldFrames only at the vocoder boundary.  include "neural_tts/neural_tts.h"  include <cmath> include <cstring> include <new> include <string> include <vector>  include "g2p/g2p.h" if defined(PICO_BUILD) include "g2p/g2p_phones.h" endif include "neural_tts/pb_decoder.h"*

#### `classifier.cc`
**Path:** `micro/stt/src/classifier.cc`
**File Doc:** *TFLM-based on-device classifier. See classifier.h for the contract.  Op set is locked to exactly what spelling_cnn.mel.int8.tflite uses today (see generate_embedded_data.py / the upstream export script): PAD, DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D, CONV_2D, ADD, SUM, FULLY_CONNECTED, RESHAPE Anything not on that list will fail at AllocateTensors() time with a clear "Op not found" error. #### `tflm_host_stub.cc`
**Path:** `micro/test-support/host/tflm_host_stub.cc`
**File Doc:** *Host (desktop) implementations of the handful of TFLM platform hooks that the modules and the micro_test.h harness reference: the MicroPrintf logging family and tflite::InitializeTarget().  The vendored pico-tflmicro provides these for the RP2350 via system_setup.cpp / debug_log.cpp, both of which call into the Pico SDK and therefore cannot be compiled on the host. For the pure-logic unit tests (feature-generation, the VAD segmenter, the STT predictor, the TTS G2P) we don't need the interpreter at all -- only logging and a no-op init -- so this tiny shim lets those tests build and run on a laptop with a normal compiler.  Interpreter-level tests (real MicroInterpreter inference) are built for the RP2350 target instead, where the full pico-tflmicro library is available.  include <cstdarg> include <cstddef> include <cstdio>*

#### `moonshine-download-smoke.cpp`
**Path:** `core/moonshine-download-smoke.cpp`
**File Doc:** *moonshine-download-smoke: a tiny CLI used by scripts/test-model-downloads.sh to verify that the native download manifests are complete. It has two modes:  moonshine-download-smoke manifest <modality> [spec...] Prints one "<url>\t<relative_path>" line per required file, resolved from the C API dependency functions (the single source of truth). The bash harness downloads each url into <root>/<relative_path>.  moonshine-download-smoke run <modality> <root> [spec...] Loads the engine from the freshly downloaded <root> and runs one trivial inference, exiting 0 on success. If a required file was missing from the manifest, loading or inference fails here - which is exactly what this test is meant to catch.  Modalities and their [spec...] arguments: stt    <language> [<model_arch>] intent <model_name> <variant> tts    <language> <voice> g2p    <language>  HTTP lives entirely in the bash harness (curl); this tool never touches the network. It only resolves manifests and exercises the on-disk load path.  include <cstdint> include <cstdio> include <cstdlib> include <cstring> include <cmath> include <filesystem> include <iostream>*

**File Doc:** *Custom ONNX Runtime operators for the ZipVoice Zipformer (domain ai.zipvoice).  Ported from the standalone ``custom_ops/swoosh_op.cc`` in the ZipVoice repo. The only structural change is that these kernels are compiled *into* libmoonshine (which already links onnxruntime) and registered on a session directly via ``zipvoice_register_custom_ops`` rather than being built as a separate shared library that ORT ``dlopen``s at runtime. This avoids loading a .so/.dll, which some platforms (e.g. iOS) make difficult.  SwooshL / SwooshR: the Zipformer activations. Exported to ONNX they decompose into ~11 element-wise nodes each; these ops collapse each activation into a single kernel. softplus(z) = log(1 + exp(z)) = max(z, 0) + log1p(exp(-|z|)) SwooshL(x)  = softplus(x - 4.0) - 0.08 * x - 0.035 SwooshR(x)  = softplus(x - 1.0) - 0.08 * x - 0.313261687 GluGate: out[..., c] = x[..., c] * sigmoid(x[..., C + c]),  C = lastdim / 2 DepthwiseConv1d: fuses Transpose -> depthwise Conv1d ('same' pad K//2) -> Transpose in [T,N,C]. BiasNorm: RMS-style norm of (x - bias) over channels, scaled by exp(log_scale). Bypass: per-channel residual lerp src_orig + (src - src_orig) * scale.  include "zipvoice-custom-ops.h"  include <algorithm> include <cmath> include <cstddef> include <vector>*

#### `fuzz-bin-tokenizer.cpp`
**Path:** `core/reliability/fuzz-bin-tokenizer.cpp`
**File Doc:** *libFuzzer harness for the binary tokenizer.  The in-memory BinTokenizer constructor parses an untrusted byte blob (a tokenizer.bin loaded from disk or an app bundle), so it is a natural fuzz target. We first build a tokenizer from the raw input, then round-trip a slice of the same input through text_to_tokens / tokens_to_text. Exceptions are the library's documented failure mode, so they are caught and ignored; only sanitizer errors (out-of-bounds reads, leaks, UB) fail the run.  include <algorithm> include <cstddef> include <cstdint> include <exception> include <string> include <vector>  include "bin-tokenizer.h"*

#### `fuzz-tensor-view.cpp`
**Path:** `core/reliability/fuzz-tensor-view.cpp`
**File Doc:** *libFuzzer harness for MoonshineTensorView construction.  The shape/dtype/data constructor forwards to moonshine_tensor_from_shape_and_dtype, which turns an (attacker-influenced) shape into an element count, a byte size, an allocation, and a memcpy. A crafted shape can overflow the size arithmetic; this harness feeds arbitrary dimensions (including huge values whose product overflows) so ASan/UBSan catch any regression in the overflow handling. Unsupported dtypes throw by design, so construction is wrapped; only sanitizer errors fail the run.  include <cstddef> include <cstdint> include <exception> include <vector>  include "moonshine-tensor-view.h"*

#### `fuzz-wav-pcm.cpp`
**Path:** `core/reliability/fuzz-wav-pcm.cpp`
**File Doc:** *libFuzzer harness for the WAV/RIFF parsers.  Both readers take a file path, so we write the fuzz input to a temporary file and parse it with (1) the first-party 16-bit PCM reader used in production and (2) the vendored header-only reader used by diarization. libFuzzer runs one input at a time in a single thread, so a per-iteration temp file is safe.  This is test-only tooling, so the raw C file APIs and free() used here are exempt from the library style rules (see core/STYLE_GUIDE.md).  include <unistd.h>  include <cstddef> include <cstdint> include <cstdlib> include <exception> include <string>  include "debug-utils.h" include "wav_pcm_float32.h"*

#### `tts-repeated-memory-test.cpp`
**Path:** `core/tts-repeated-memory-test.cpp`
**File Doc:** *Repeated-use memory regression test for the text-to-speech synthesizers.  The transcriber has a long-stream memory test (transcriber-streaming-memory- test.cpp); this is the TTS analogue. It exercises each available engine (Kokoro, Piper, ZipVoice, English only) through the public C API in two loops that probe the two distinct leak surfaces:  * "synth"  - one synthesizer, many moonshine_text_to_speech() calls (each output buffer freed). Catches leaks in the inference / G2P / per-call allocation path. * "reload" - repeatedly create and free the synthesizer handle. Catches leaks in model load / teardown and the handle table.  TTS exposes no internal retained-byte accessor (unlike the transcriber's stream_vad_completed_audio_bytes), so the signal here is process RSS: the test samples resident memory after every iteration and fails on sustained, post-warmup growth using the same regression heuristic as the transcriber test. onnxruntime arena allocators grow during warmup and then plateau, so the warmup window is skipped and only a persistent upward trend is treated as a regression.  The bundled TTS data (core/moonshine-tts/data) is required. Pass its path as argv[1], or run with a working directory from which it can be discovered (repo root, test-assets/, or core/build). Engines whose assets are absent are skipped. Invoked from scripts/reliability-remote.sh.  define DOCTEST_CONFIG_IMPLEMENT include <doctest.h>  include <algorithm>*

**Functions:**
- `read_rss_kb` (line 53) `size_t read_rss_kb()`
- `median` (line 89) `size_t median(std::vector<size_t> values)`
- `env_size` (line 98) `size_t env_size(const char *name, size_t default_value)`
- `detect_continual_growth` (line 117) `bool detect_continual_growth(const std::vector<size_t> &samples,
                             siz...` - *Mirrors transcriber-streaming-memory-test's detector: fits a line to the post-warmup samples and reports sustained growth only when the median gain, the fraction of non-decreasing steps, and the fitted slope all clear their thresholds. This tolerates one-off jumps and allocator caching while still catching an unbounded per-iteration leak.*
- `create_synth` (line 222) `int32_t create_synth(const EngineSpec &spec)`
- `synth_once` (line 235) `bool synth_once(int32_t handle, size_t text_index)`
- `reload_strict` (line 247) `bool reload_strict()`

                      const st...` - *Runs `iterations` of `body`, sampling RSS after each, and checks for sustained post-warmup growth. Reports the regression summary either way for context. When `advisory` is true a positive finding is logged but does not fail the run (RSS across repeated model load/free is dominated by allocator / OS page retention rather than a reliable leak signal); otherwise it is a hard gate.*
